0.content:
A Brief History of the Pale Starborn (also: Brief History of the Pale Starborn, Pale Starborn history): A single-volume fae chronicle sold at Mimisbrunnr Books in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai (6.3). It records Emperor Monomakh's war that broke the Volkodlak king Miscislav, and Tsaritsa Anastasya's later takeover of the fae princes' power.

Lore: In the 428th Cycle Miscislav of the Volkodlak demanded huge tribute from Emperor Monomakh, lost three battles and died; the Emperor became the Belyi Tsar. In the 799th Cycle Anastasya was crowned and the fae princes lost their rule.

1.comment: A Day Carved From Rising Winds
1.content:
A Day Carved From Rising Winds (also: Windborne Flower's Spruchdichtung, Dawn's Brilliant Oath, A Note in Spring's Leich, Heldenepos's Unspoken Tale, Minnesang of Love and Lament, Blessing of Pastoral Winds, Resolve of Pastoral Winds): A Day Carved From Rising Winds is a 4- and 5-star artifact set (added in 6.3) about the old uprising against the storm god Decarabian in ancient Mondstadt and the birth of the wind god who became Barbatos. Its pieces are an oath of the Gunnhildr clan, a guard's laid-down sword, a bard's last song, an archer's final arrow and a huntress's doomed devotion to her king. It is obtained in Moonchild's Treasures in Nod-Krai.

Lore: The texts retell the fall of the tyrant of storms in Old Mondstadt and the rise of a wind god, in verse. The bard who gave his song and life, and the freed people who followed, are never named.

2.content: A Legend of Sword (also: Legend of Sword): A Legend of Sword is a six-volume light novel sold in Inazuma through Yae Publishing House. It is a space-war epic with a swordsman strategist, and part of it flashes back to a ronin helping a village against bandits.

3.content:
A Teaspoon of Transcendence (also: Teaspoon of Transcendence): A Teaspoon of Transcendence is a 5-star claymore. Its description calls it an object of fantasy with countless definitions in an endless sea of stories: no real difference between a hero's holy sword and a princess's teaspoon, or between a cold clockspring and the key to the gates of transcendence. Its text is a conversation between Sandrone and Alain. Added in Version 6.7.

Lore: The text opens with a line that heroes of different stories find different holy swords and face different nemeses, then shows Sandrone closing a storybook and asking Alain why heroes always win.

Owners: No in-game text names an owner. The wiki trivia notes that Sandrone is seen wielding the unascended claymore in her Character Trailer, which makes her the closest known association.

4.content:
A Thousand Blazing Suns (also: Thousand Blazing Suns, Sunset Reignites the Dawn): A Thousand Blazing Suns is a 5-star claymore from Natlan, a greatsword that dazzles like the rising sun. Its story is a legend of the first human Pyro Archon, who took the Sacred Flame and chose to keep fighting the Abyss.

Lore: When the great dragon bowed its head, the leader of the mortals reached the primal flame, and the god who pronounced death showed him the Abyss devouring all life. He understood that a new war had begun.

Owners: No wielder is named in the item text; association with any character is a gameplay convention.

5.content:
A Thousand Floating Dreams: A Thousand Floating Dreams is a 5-star catalyst from Sumeru, a lamp whose emerald light carries "a song of ancient days". Its item story is a lyrical tale of the girl who had never known "light", who hears the Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's whisper in a dream as a palace crumbles and later walks out of the dreams into a real dawn. The wiki reads the girl as the Dendro Archon Nahida.

Lore: At the moment the palace crumbled, the girl who had never known "light" heard the Greater Lord's whisper inside a dream. A verdant lamp then shows stories: an emerald-eyed dancer kissing nectar-soaked silk, brightly coloured fish in pearly water, a moonlight musician guiding the Jinn's torches, and a sailor seeking a voice from a dream and the blooming gardens of a far shore.

Owners: No in-world owner is named. Nahida is shown wielding it in her Collected Miscellany video and her Genius Invokation TCG character card.

6.content: A Thousand Nights (also: Torn Page: A Thousand Nights): A Thousand Nights is a six-volume collection of torn pages found in Sumeru's deserts. Its stories were gathered by a wandering researcher during the Cataclysm and only a fragment survives.

7.content:
Absolution (also: Deathly Pact): Absolution is a 5-star rapier once wielded by a deceiver who had forsaken everything. In the past it served mainly as a tool when he had to disguise his identity.

Lore: Thompson Reed is a young man from the Fleuve Cendre who took his mother's lesson of sincerity and diligence as a lie, after learning she lay buried there. He decided that lying and surviving were what mattered, and used costumes and masks to climb.

Owners: Thompson Reed, per the description. No present-day owner is named.

8.content: Aerosiderite (also: Black meteoric iron, Grain of Aerosiderite, Piece of Aerosiderite, Bit of Aerosiderite, Chunk of Aerosiderite): Aerosiderite is a rare black ore used to ascend weapons, sold in Liyue and gathered at the Hidden Palace of Lianshan Formula. Its item texts say it came from a black meteor that fell beyond Liyue's Sea of Clouds, dropped to vanquish a monster. The monster's tainted blood stained it, so it no longer holds the pure power of Rex Lapis.

9.content:
Akasha Terminal (also: Neo Akasha Terminal, Akasha earpiece): The Akasha Terminal is a small leaf-shaped device that hovers over the user's left ear and links them to the Akasha, Sumeru's shared information network. Concentrate on a subject and the Akasha supplies what the user's clearance allows. It was a daily tool for most of Sumeru until the system was shut down after the events of Chapter III.

Lore: The network lets people look up information, send messages and share documents. A user whose clearance is too low simply gets silence.

10.content: Akuoumaru (also: Akuou-maru, Akuou's sword, Akuou's blade): Akuoumaru is a four-star claymore, part of the Watatsumi series, and the beloved sword of the Watatsumi warrior known to his foes as "Akuou". Item text calls the blade huge and majestic yet surprisingly easy to wield. It belonged to a young man whom the people of Watatsumi named Touzannou, a champion of Orobashi's war against the Raiden Shogun's forces.

11.content:
Alley Hunter: Alley Hunter is a 4-star bow of the Alley series, an opulent black longbow. Its story belongs to Mondstadt's aristocratic age: a noble house's hunting bow fell into the hands of a gentleman thief who was never caught, and used it to shoot crowns off noble heads without a sound. The tale ends bittersweetly, with a witch he loved branded and vanished and the thief fled across the sea.

Lore: The bow passed from a noble house to a gentleman thief who was never caught. He shot crowns from noble heads in silence, cut through tightened bonds and disarmed pursuing soldiers. He once vowed to bring light to a darkened age and to bring justice, riches and gladness to the oppressed.

Owners: An unnamed noble house first; then the gentleman thief. No present-day character is established as owning it.

12.content: Amenoma Kageuchi (also: Hakuen Michimitsu Amenoma kageuchi, Amenoma shadow forge): Amenoma Kageuchi is a four-star sword forged in Inazuma, described as one of the "kageuchi" copies of the famed blade "Hakuen Michimitsu Amenoma". Iwakura Douin, founding patriarch of the Iwakura clan, gave it to the Saimon clan as thanks for caring for him while he lived in seclusion in Konda Village. Its item text is mostly about the Iwakura secret technique Tengu Sweeper.

13.content: Amethyst Lump (also: Violet Crystal): Amethyst Lump is an uncut violet crystal that, by its in-game description, can only be found in Inazuma. It is mined from Violet Crystal ore deposits and treated as a raw forging ore.

14.content: Amos' Bow (also: Amos's Bow, the bow of Amos): Amos' Bow is an extremely ancient five-star bow from Old Mondstadt, when the land was still a wasteland under the God of Storms Decarabian. It is named for Amos, a huntress who loved Decarabian, then turned against him and fired an arrow at him from the top of his tower. Item text says the bow still holds power although its owner is long gone, and that it draws strength from all things in the world.

15.content:
Anecdota Septentrionalis (also: Anecdota Septentrionalis (scroll), Northern Anecdotes): Anecdota Septentrionalis is a three-volume ancient Remurian scroll found in the ruins of the Faded Castle. Its narrator states from the start that everything he writes is invented, then recounts a voyage to find the edge of the ocean. The in-game description says there is no way to verify its words.

Lore: Vol. 1: The narrator mocks writers who insist their stories are true, using the example of Xanthus Talassii filius, who wrote about northern barbarians and a king he calls a knight, though the narrator says he never left Capitolium. He then declares his own tale a total fabrication. His crew sails north to see the edge of the ocean, sails 79 days without land, and on the 80th day is attacked by bandits on giant birds who ask for potatoes. Warriors on armoured Blubberbeasts rescue them. The knights look like bipedal vishaps.

16.content: Anemo Gnosis (also: Barbatos's Gnosis, Venti's Gnosis, Gnosis of the Anemo Archon): The Anemo Gnosis is the Gnosis of Barbatos (Venti), the Anemo Archon: a gleaming, chess-piece-like divine focus that sat inside his chest and, in his words, resonates directly with Celestia. At the end of the Prologue (1.0) the Fatui Harbinger Signora ambushed Venti in Mondstadt and tore it out. As of 7.1 it is one of six Gnoses held by the Tsaritsa in Snezhnaya.

17.content:
Angelos' Heptades (also: Angelos Heptades): Angelos' Heptades is a 5-star catalyst in the Hexerei series, described as a golden box as splendid as the light of the heavens that, according to legend, once belonged to a divine envoy of the Eternal Court. Its text tells how the youngest angel was hidden from the angels' rebellion, then chose to cast off divinity and wander among mortals. Added in Version 6.6.

Lore: The envoy was a newborn girl whose elder sisters protected her; she later gave up her divinity and her old powers, kept human form, and walked the mortal world alone.

Owners: The weapon "once belonged to" a divine envoy of the Eternal Court. The wiki reads the envoy as Nicole, the youngest angel; Nicole was the featured character on the Version 6.6 banner running with this weapon, but no text declares she holds it now.

18.content: Aqua Simulacra: Aqua Simulacra is a five-star bow of Liyue whose color is unpredictable: under light it takes on a lustrous, watery blue. Its item text says it can summon water and uses water as a lesson, that water has no fixed form and is at once the gentlest and keenest of substances. The story ties the lesson to Yelan, who received it from an elderly senior before she worked for Ningguang of the Jade Chamber.

19.content:
Aquila Favonia (also: Vennessa's sword): Aquila Favonia is the sword of Vennessa, the enslaved foreign gladiator who led Mondstadt's revolt against its tyrannical old nobles about a thousand years ago and founded the Knights of Favonius and the Church of Favonius. Its item text calls it "the soul of the Knights of Favonius" and says it still calls on the winds of swift justice. Its name means "Eagle of the West Wind", echoing Vennessa's later title, the Falcon of the West.

Lore: The sword's story says everyone knew "the falcon's" protection was a blessing of Favonius, but few knew that this blessing came from a distant tribe. Under the old nobles, an exiled foreign fighter was enslaved in Mondstadt; she refused to kneel to injustice, overthrew the nobles, founded a chivalric order and the Church, and was eventually blessed to walk with the gods. The sword witnessed all her hardships and deeds.

Owners: Vennessa (the Falcon of the West, first Grand Master and first Dandelion Knight of the Knights of Favonius) is the only named wielder.

20.content:
Archaic Petra (also: Flower of Creviced Cliff, Feather of Jagged Peaks, Sundial of Enduring Jade, Goblet of Chiseled Crag, Mask of Solitude Basalt): Archaic Petra is a 4- and 5-star Geo artifact set (1.0) made of Liyue folk legends about Rex Lapis, the Lord of Geo: flowers from stone, a giant hawk of rock and jade, sundials, wine vessels and a solemn basalt mask. Its Chinese name means roughly 'ancient boulder'.

Lore: Each piece retells a legend about Rex Lapis, the Lord of Geo, always framed as a saying ('they say') rather than recorded fact.

21.content:
Ash-Graven Drinking Horn (also: Ash-Graven Horn, Tupac's Grip): The Ash-Graven Drinking Horn is a 4-star catalyst from Natlan: a ritual drinking vessel handed down among the Meztli, said to have been the treasure of the giant hero Tupac. Its story is a banquet song about him.

Lore: A minstrel sings of the ancient ancestor Tupac, huge as a mountain. The young hero Tenoch, furious, would have challenged him for the horn; Tupac, laughing, would have answered that it rightfully belonged to him and his homeland's kin.

Owners: Legend ties it to Tupac, the giant of the Meztli, who never used it. Later holders are not named.

22.content:
Astral Vulture's Crimson Plumage (also: Crimson Plumage, The Moonring Sighted): Astral Vulture's Crimson Plumage is a 5-star bow: an ancient longbow crested with red feathers, a sacred relic of Natlan's Flower-Feather Clan handed down through generations.

Lore: The Flower-Feather elder, who only pretended to obey the usurper king, banished a young man to help him escape capture, because he wished to protect the Saurians. His red eyes reflected only the cold aqua moon ring above him.

Owners: The Flower-Feather Clan keeps it as a sacred relic; no individual wielder is named.

23.content:
Athame Artis: Athame Artis is a 5-star sword in the Hexerei series, described as a precious sword the Day King gave to the brave hero in a little witch's story, only for the witch to take it and defeat the hero herself. Its text is a fairy-tale in which the witch destroys a perpetual motion machine to keep a dying planet alive. Added in Version 6.2.

Lore: A little witch arrives at the Day King's palace as twilight takes the kingdom; the story follows her through the following night.

Owners: The item belongs to the story's Day King, who gave it to a hero; no real-world owner is named in canon. The wiki says the weapon is tailored to Durin.

24.content:
Aubade of Morningstar and Moon (also: Moonlit Offering's Opulent Dream, Moonlit Offering's Parting Light, Moonlit Offering's Final Hour, Moonlit Offering's Libation, Moonlit Offering's Silver Crown): Aubade of Morningstar and Moon is a 4- and 5-star artifact set dropped in the Moonchild's Treasures domain in Nod-Krai. Its five pieces (Moonlit Offering's ...) carry item text about an ancient age when three moons guided the heavens, how mortals came to worship them, and how two of them fell, ending an age called Eternity. Mechanically it supports Lunar reactions.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: the 2-piece bonus gives +80 Elemental Mastery; the 4-piece bonus boosts Lunar reaction damage while the wearer is off-field.

25.content:
Azurelight: Azurelight is a 5-star sword, once pure white like a dawn star and now tinted deep blue. Its item text is an angel's sermon urging the angels to defy the Heavenly Principles and entrust the world to humanity. Added in Version 5.7.

Lore: The text is spoken by one who once taught that the heavens' laws must never be questioned, until starlight on a white stone mountain showed them a coming sunrise.

Owners: Canon gives no owner or wielder in the item text. It debuted in Version 5.7 during the same period as Skirk's character banner, but no source cited here says it belongs to her.

26.content:
Ballads of the Squire (also: Squire's Ballads): A two-volume Mondstadt book of ballads handed down from the aristocratic period and said to come from Ragnvindr, the Dawn Knight. Volume 1 follows his time as a knight's squire; Volume 2 his friendship with a sword-dancer.

Lore: Vol. 1: a squire patrols Mondstadt at night, ignoring the knights' boasts of starlit glory and seeing only the suffering of the poor under the aristocracy. Vol. 2: a chained dancer of the Wanderer's Troupe arrives, challenges the aristocrats, and dies in the arena; a nameless knight buries her sword.

27.content:
Beacon of the Reed Sea: Beacon of the Reed Sea is a 5-star claymore of the Deshret series. The in-game description calls it a large, flat-tipped sword designed as the weapon of an ancient king or some ceremonial instrument. Its story is told through a blind wandering poet who gathers the desert's ballads after the Lord of Sand sank into the desert with dreams in his embrace.

Lore: In an age when kingdoms rose and fell like mushrooms and sandcastles, the blind poet, once of privileged birth, crosses the sea of desert and collects ballads from its scattered people. He hears of the fall of his homeland, of the prince who blinded him finally crushing the overwhelmed throne, of a dancer who helped one man after another become king and then buried them in sandstorms, and of springs replaced by sand and nations shrunk to villages and tribes.

Owners: No owner is named. Dehya is shown wielding a claymore of this kind in her Genius Invokation TCG character card and in the Sumeru promotional video (wiki trivia).

28.content:
Beyond the Chrysalis: Beyond the Chrysalis is a 5-star sword. Its description calls it a longsword brimming with light and color, as weightless as a butterfly when brandished, once used by a certain individual to break bonds. Its text is the story of the eldest daughter of a Vila noble house in Snezhnaya who ended a rebellion against the Tsaritsa and then asked to lose her name. Added in Version 7.1.

Lore: Before she lost her last name, the world knew her as the eldest daughter of the Strivozhas, a Vila noble house.

Owners: Canon does not name an owner. The text tells the story of Gluvasha, a Vila who gave up her house name; a link to the sword is only inferred from the item description about breaking bonds.

29.content:
Biography of Gunnhildr (also: Gunnhildr's Biography): Biography of Gunnhildr is a Mondstadt history book written by the modern historian Eckhard Gunnhildr. It retells legends of the clan's apical ancestor, Gunnhildr: a chieftain's daughter whose prayer won a wind spirit's protection for her wandering people, and who later honoured Barbatos after the fall of Decarabian's tyranny. It ends by praising the clan's service to Mondstadt today.

Lore: Three thousand years ago (the book's figure), Mondstadt was a frozen wasteland and Decarabian, the Lord of the Tower, fought the North Wind King Andrius. Gunnhildr's father, leader of a nomadic clan, had left Decarabian's service because of his despotism and led his people out into blizzards. Gunnhildr prayed, a wind spirit answered, and she gained the power to protect. She later became clan leader and first priestess, and after Barbatos freed the tyrant's subjects she placed laurels on him.

30.content:
Blackcliff Longsword: Blackcliff Longsword is a 4-star sword of the Blackcliff series, described in game as a sword of blackstone with a dark crimson glow on its black blade. It was wrought by the master craftsman Han Wu from crystallized blackcliff, a rare stone he fetched from the Chasm. It has been in the game since Version 1.0.

Lore: Blackcliff is a rare stone; the longsword is cut from its crystallized form and is said to slice through gold and jade easily.

31.content:
Blackmarrow Lantern (also: Token of Covenant): Blackmarrow Lantern is a 4-star catalyst of the Rossum series: a lantern with a faint ghostly glow, held in a midnight-black alloy that looks like interlocking bones.

Lore: The item story opens with a parable: power is a great edifice, and sheer chance alone decides which brick becomes foundation and which becomes spire. A single brick that refuses the false order can bring the whole building down.

Owners: No owner is named. The lantern is tied to the Godfather, and the secret organization that revered it is not identified.

32.content:
Blade of Atonement (also: Repentance and Redemption): Blade of Atonement is a 4-star claymore of Snezhnaya's Kuznets series, described as a greatsword passed down by the Luchkin and said to be fit only for the bravest warrior. Its story is that of Rafalovich, a silent warrior who once served the Burner of Cities and now carries the weight of what he did.

Lore: Rafalovich is a Volkodlak warrior who once believed the Burner of Cities' promise of a pure, joyful new land. He fought for her without mercy, then abandoned that life and now bears a face wound that never healed and a vow of silence and solitude.

Owners: Rafalovich is the warrior of the story. The description says the greatsword was passed down by the Luchkin. No modern owner is named.

33.content:
Blizzard Strayer (also: Snowswept Memory, Icebreaker's Resolve, Frozen Homeland's Demise, Frost-Weaved Dignity, Broken Rime's Echo): Blizzard Strayer is a Cryo artifact set (4 and 5 star, added 1.2) from Dragonspine. Its pieces tell of the Icebreaker, a quiet hero from a mountain city lost to endless winter, who left with the hopes of its people and was never heard of again. The wiki connects it to Imunlaukr and the fallen nation of Sal Vindagnyr. It drops in the Peak of Vindagnyr domain.

Lore: A hero left his snow-sealed city to find salvation. A maiden who painted frescoes waited for him. He did not return in time and was branded a deserter; his deeds were forgotten, though the frost-flower never withered.

34.content:
Bloodsoaked Ruins (also: Mournful Tribute, Requiem of Ruin): A long spear tainted black by unrelenting battle, glowing faintly beneath the ghostly blue light of a lantern-fire. A 5-star polearm from Version 6.0, shown in Flins's hands.

Lore: A Snezhnayan folk tale says the King of Midsommar Oak, who brought warmth, was accidentally slain by his elder brother, the King of Winter Icelea, and so the world has known unrelenting winter. The spear's story sets a human tragedy beside it.

Owners: Flins is shown wielding it in official art and trailers; the item text itself names no owner.

35.content:
Bloodstained Chivalry (also: Bloodstained Flower of Iron, Bloodstained Black Plume, Bloodstained Final Hour, Bloodstained Chevalier's Goblet, Bloodstained Iron Mask, Bloodstained Knight): Bloodstained Chivalry is a Physical artifact set (4 and 5 star, added 1.0). Its five pieces tell the downfall of a righteous knight: he began as a white knight who rescued a maiden, killed so much in the name of justice that he came to see himself as a monster, and finally went to the fallen kingdom to die. The wiki names him as Roland; the texts say only 'the Bloodstained Knight'.

Lore: A white knight rescued a maiden, wanted no reward but chivalry, and later killed so much that he could not tell his own blood from his enemies'. He became the Bloodstained Knight and died in the lair of monsters in the ancient kingdom.

36.content:
Breeze Amidst the Forest (also: Breeze in Woods): Breeze Amidst the Forest is a two-volume Mondstadt book. Vol. 1 is an anthology of bard ballads, including the tale of the young Wind Dragon who sought to be understood and became a protector of Mondstadt. Vol. 2 adds excerpts about the Four Winds and the battle between Dvalin and the corrupted dragon Durin. The compiler warns that bards embellish.

Lore: In the ballad, a young dragon graced by Anemo is born in the high heavens, descends and tries to understand humans, but villagers throw stones and farmers curse him. He hears the Holy Lyre der Himmel, the Anemo Archon's lyre, and lands beside the bard. The people panic because dragons and archons never agreed, yet the dragon learns human speech and the bard's songs and stays. Later generations count him among the Four Winds.

37.content:
Calamity of Eshu (also: Sanhaj's ritual sword, Eshu's Calamity): The Calamity of Eshu is a 4-star sword from Natlan: the curved ceremonial blade of Sanhaj, the great high priest of the Masters of the Night-Wind. Legend says he used it in rituals that blurred the boundary between the Night Kingdom and the living world.

Lore: A child who barely spoke for years was told by a ritual elder that half his soul had been lost in the night flames. On his birthday he walked into the stony wastes to find it, with only the Iktomisaur Mahamba willing to go with him.

Owners: Sanhaj's ritual sword, now kept by the Masters of the Night-Wind's chief.

38.content: Calamity Queller: Calamity Queller is a five-star polearm of Liyue, a keenly honed weapon forged from a strange aqua-colored crystal, whose faint blue light seems to whisper of countless past matters. Item text says it was made from materials not of this world, passed through many loyal but unfortunate hands and was lost with the Yaksha who wielded it at the end of the Cataclysm. Shenhe is shown wielding it in official art.

39.content:
Cashflow Supervision (also: Golden Blood-Tide): Cashflow Supervision is a 5-star catalyst: a floating device that can monitor certain phenomena. After being abandoned, it was picked up and modified for other purposes.

Lore: The text argues that the flow of money traces the arteries of the world and that humanity should master currency, not be enslaved by it. A certain person (the wiki links Pantalone) cannot accept that the corner of the world in which money flows was chosen and defined by a god, which the text points at as Liyue and Rex Lapis.

Owners: No owner is named. The device was abandoned, then picked up and modified.

40.content: Cecilia (also: Cecilia flower, Cecilias): The Cecilia is a beautiful flower of Mondstadt that grows only where harsh winds blow. It is a Mondstadt local specialty, gathered on Starsnatch Cliff, and is the favourite flower of Venti the bard.

41.content:
Celestial Gift (also: Heavensent Fragrance, Heavensent Demise, Heavensent Decree, Heavensent Reward, Heavensent Crown): Celestial Gift is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from the Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind domain in Mondstadt. Its Heavensent pieces tell of a star-faring civilisation that watched the cosmos die, a voyager who woke from the void to find a shrouded world, and the eldest angel's rebellion in the frozen north against the heavens. Mechanically it gives Energy Recharge and team Elemental DMG Bonus.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: 2-piece +20% Energy Recharge; 4-piece gives a team Elemental DMG Bonus after an Elemental Skill, strengthened by Hexerei.

42.content:
Cinnabar Spindle: Cinnabar Spindle is a 4-star sword, in-game description "a sword made from materials that do not belong in this world," whose power might withstand the corruption of a venom that could corrode a mighty dragon. It was the reward weapon of the limited-time event Shadows Amidst Snowstorms in Version 2.3, a Dragonspine event in which Albedo appears; it ran 2021-11-25 to 2021-12-13.

Lore: The text is an exhortation: separate the dust in the flames with joy and extract the exquisite from the crude, for all things in the universe come from a single source and may be derived from a single thought.

43.content:
Clash of Kings: Clash of Kings is a 4-star catalyst: a golden box lavishly inlaid with precious jewels that houses a game much beloved by the kings of the sands. Its story is a legend of three gods who, bored in a formless world, create a new one and play a board game over it.

Lore: The story is told as a legend. Before anything existed there were only three gods in a world without beginning or end: Valor, with unlimited power; Cunning, with unlimited wisdom and guile; and Nature. Valor and Cunning fought endlessly without result, so Nature proposed making a new world and deciding the winner with dice, since even gods cannot change the dice.

Owners: No owner is named, and no character is recorded wielding it.

44.content:
Cloudforged (also: Crag-Chiseled Forge): Cloudforged is a 4-star bow added in Version 4.7. Its in-game description calls it a prototype of a standard-issue weapon that the Yuheng commissioned from Blackcliff Forge, after analysing the ancient mechanisms that guarded the adeptal abode on Mount Tianheng. It was a reward of the limited-time event Mutual Security Enhancing Simulation.

Lore: The item text says the ancients called Mount Tianheng full of gems and the Chasm rich in jade, and that Liyue's key mining and smelting works are in Blackcliff Forge, carved into Tianheng itself.

45.content:
Conch Echoes (also: Conch Echoes (book)): Conch Echoes is a two-volume book of Nod-Krai, sold by Dhabit at Mimisbrunnr Books in Nasha Town. Its in-game description calls it a very old tale of children who spoke while holding conch shells in the empty frontier wastelands, by an author long forgotten. The story is about who deserves to lead and what happens when power is taken by force.

Lore: Vol. 1: Exiled children, who secretly call their place of banishment the "Outlands", have outlived the adults who made them work as slaves. They agreed a pact that whoever holds a conch, taken in secret from the beach, has the right to speak and that a clever leader would be chosen to hold it. On the thirtieth night a handsome young man with a blade demands the conch from the smallest boy, "Shorty". He argues that he earned the most and holds the blade, so he will command everyone. Shorty hands it over, walks into the forest, and seems to smirk as he goes.

46.content: Crane's Echoing Call (also: Cranes Echoing Call): Crane's Echoing Call is a five-star catalyst of Liyue, described in game as a fan carved from pure jade with an ancient aura of adeptal energy swirling around it. Its item story tells of a distant time before Liyue Harbor existed, when refugees begged the adepti for shelter while a horde of maddened monsters pursued them, and how the adeptus Cloud Retainer is said to have saved them. Xianyun, who is Cloud Retainer, wields it.

47.content: Crimson Agate (also: Crimson Agates): Crimson Agate is a crystal found on Dragonspine, the snowbound mountain of Mondstadt. It forms when concentrated life force combines with an energy unique to Dragonspine, and it is ideal nourishment for the Frostbearing Tree.

48.content:
Crimson Moon's Semblance (also: Crimson Moon's Semblance polearm): Crimson Moon's Semblance is a 5-star polearm (released in Version 4.6) whose text recalls an ancient Khaenri'ahn dynasty that revered the crimson moon. Its description calls it a keen-edged weapon with a luster as dazzling as the crimson moon, once regarded by that dynasty as a ritual object that could bridge two worlds. Arlecchino is its signature wielder in gameplay.

Lore: The item story is a sombre account of Khaenri'ah's old royal clan and the Crimson Moon, not of the weapon's own forging.

Owners: Arlecchino, the Fourth Fatui Harbinger and head of the House of the Hearth, is its signature wielder.

key: Crimson Witch of Flames artifact set
49.content:
Crimson Witch of Flames (also: Crimson Witch of Flames artifact set, Witch's Flower of Blaze, Witch's Ever-Burning Plume, Witch's End Time, Witch's Heart Flames, Witch's Scorching Hat): Crimson Witch of Flames is a Pyro artifact set (4 and 5 star) built around the story of a young woman who lost her hopes and loved ones in a calamity and became a witch who burned monsters and demons. Its texts call her 'the Crimson Witch of Flame'. Later canon (Archon Quest, 2.1) identifies her as the Fatui Harbinger Signora, once a maiden of Mondstadt. The set is earned in the Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula.

Lore: The texts follow the 'Crimson Witch of Flame' from a maiden with a bright future to a hunter of monsters. A crisis centuries ago ended her hopes; from the ashes she burned away her pain with fire.

50.content:
Cryo Gnosis (also: Tsaritsa's Gnosis, Gnosis of the Cryo Archon): The Cryo Gnosis is the Gnosis of the Cryo Archon. It is held by Anastasya, the Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya, and is the only one of the seven Gnoses that never had to be collected by the Fatui. Like every Gnosis, it is a divine focus that resembles a chess piece and strengthens its bearer's elemental power. Each Archon's Gnosis also links them to Celestia.

Owners: Current holder: Anastasya, the Tsaritsa and Cryo Archon, at Zapolyarny Palace in Snezhnograd.

51.content: Crystal Chunk (also: Crystal Chunks, Crystal Ore): Crystal Chunk is a turquoise crystal, an uncut ore taken from Crystal Ore nodes in caves, mines and mountains across Teyvat. Its item text says only professional craftsmanship can bring out its true value. Smiths use it in forging, chiefly for Mystic Enhancement Ore.

52.content: Crystal Core (also: Crystal Cores, crystalfly core): Crystal Core is the core of a crystal butterfly, a crystalfly. Its item text says it absorbs elemental energy that has escaped into the atmosphere. It is obtained by catching a crystalfly, not by fighting it.

53.content:
Customs of Liyue (also: Liyue Customs): Customs of Liyue is a three-volume book about Liyue's traditions, originally compiled by Fadhlan, a scholar from Sumeru living in Liyue, then edited by local scholars and published. It is described as one of Liyue's bestsellers. The volumes cover the wedding flower ball, the Rite of Descension in which the Geo Archon receives his people, and the cultural place of the Silk Flower and its perfumes.

Lore: - Vol. 1, Flower Ball: at Liyue weddings the bride tosses a flower ball to the guests; catching it is said to bring a year of good luck. Wealthier families use silk balls, poorer families paper or cloth.
- Vol. 2, Receiving God: the Rite of Descension is the most iconic Liyue ceremony, at which the Geo Archon descends to deliver his proclamations. In the Qixing era a member of the Qixing hosts it.
- Vol. 3, Silk Flowers: the Silk Flower is used for silk and perfume. Rural legend credits an adeptus on Mt. Aocang with teaching mortals perfume making, and the flower is a symbol of Rex Lapis.

54.content:
Dawning Frost (also: Nocturnal Dreams, Dawning Frost catalyst): A silver-forged ritual vessel, pure and without blemish, said to be a sacred relic passed down among the priestesses of the far north. A 4-star catalyst of the Frostmoon Scion series from Version 6.1.

Lore: The item text is a warning and a dream: a mother tells her child, Avrelian, never to set foot in Nod-Krai and not to be taken in by "that fool's dream of Elysium".

Owners: No wielder is named; the description ties it to the priestesses of the far north.

55.content: Deathmatch (also: Deathmatch polearm, the gladiator's spear): Deathmatch is a four-star crimson polearm, part of the Gnostic Hymn series from the Battle Pass. Its item story follows a gladiator who fought for blood, then for the young master he loved, and who died by the blade of a red-haired maiden at his last performance. The wiki identifies that maiden as Vennessa and the master as Eberhart.

56.content:
Deepwood Memories (also: Labyrinth Wayfarer, Scholar of Vines, A Time of Insight, Lamp of the Lost, Laurel Coronet): Deepwood Memories is a Sumeru rainforest artifact set (Version 3.0, Spire of Solitary Enlightenment domain). Its five pieces are fragments of old forest legends: a labyrinth of roots and water, a lord of the forest and the maiden who inherited his crown, a huntress with a white bow, and friends who fought forgetting.

Lore: When the lord of the forest was born, the king of trees gave them a crown, which passed to the first maiden to follow in the lord's footsteps. She took in lost children and taught them the hunt, the walk through dreams and love for the forest's plants and creatures. Some became guardians who patrolled the woods and lit bonfires against the dark. One stayed behind, hunting the shadows until she dreamed a great dream of the labyrinth and hunt that covered every other dream of the forest, and then she disappeared with it.

57.content:
Dendro Gnosis (also: Gnosis of Sumeru, Dendro Archon's Gnosis, Kusanali's Gnosis, Nahida's Gnosis): The Dendro Gnosis is Sumeru's Gnosis, one of seven chess-piece-like divine foci held by The Seven, carried inside the Archon's chest. Greater Lord Rukkhadevata used it to build and power the Akasha. In 3.2 Nahida (Lesser Lord Kusanali) gave it to the Fatui Harbinger Dottore in exchange for knowledge about the "false sky", and shut the Akasha down. Dottore brought it to the Tsaritsa in Snezhnaya, and as of 7.1 she holds it with five other Gnoses. Nahida is still the Dendro Archon without it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Tsaritsa (Anastasya) holds it in Snezhnaya, one of her six Gnoses; only the Pyro Gnosis is missing.

key: The First Days of the City of Kings
58.content:
Desert Pavilion Chronicle (also: The First Days of the City of Kings, End of the Golden Realm, Timepiece of the Lost Path, Defender of the Enchanting Dream, Legacy of the Desert High-Born): Desert Pavilion Chronicle is a Sumeru desert artifact set (Version 3.3, City of Gold domain). Its five item texts form one poem, recited by an old blind poet, about Gurabad: the shepherd Ormazd made vassal king with the Jinni Liloupar's help, his slide into tyranny, Liloupar's revenge, the city's fall, and the desert splintering into seven states.

Lore: Legend says the Lord of the Sands, after his lover's death, made a pact with humanity through the Jinn: only incorruptible mortals could serve as vassal-kings. The Jinni Liloupar chose the shepherd Ormazd, warned him that her blessing carried "sharp retribution", and watched him ignore it. He united the clans, was crowned, and made Gurabad the mortals' capital.

59.content:
Dialogues of the Desert Sages: Dialogues of the Desert Sages is a 4-star polearm: a caduceus symbolising the glory of alchemy, made from special alloys. Its story names the seven sages of King Deshret and tells how the Crocodile King and the Ibis King wagered on a transmutation, with the sage Hermanubis ruling that the two powers must balance.

Lore: King Deshret's seven sages vanished long ago; their deeds are blown away and only their names, carved in stone, remain, now eroded to golden grains of sand. The text lists four: the Goat King (Heryshaf), right hand of the King and head of the sages; the sun-bound bird that was the King's soul, Bennu; the human-headed lioness that was the King's will, Shesepankh; and the dragon Al-Apep, who obtained the King's flesh and blood and never counted himself among the Seven. These four have nothing to do with the story that follows.

Owners: No owner is named, and no character is recorded wielding it.

60.content:
Diary of Roald the Adventurer (also: Roald's Diary, Roald's diaries, Adventurer Roald's diary): Diary of Roald the Adventurer is an 11-volume book collection of travel diaries by Roald, a seasoned adventurer. He walks through Liyue (Sal Terrae, Qingce Village, Jueyun Karst, Yaoguang Shoal, Guyun Stone Forest), climbs Dragonspine, waits out the Sakoku Decree in Ritou and ends on Tsurumi Island in Inazuma. Each entry pairs a travel log with local legends and a note to himself not to lose the diary again, which he keeps doing.

Lore: Roald records places and the legends told about them, from the God of Salt's fall at Sal Terrae (Vol. 1) and the sea monster Chi at Qingce to Dragonspine, Ritou and Tsurumi Island.

61.content:
Disaster and Remorse (also: Dolorous Stroke): Disaster and Remorse is a 5-star Hexerei-series polearm, described as forged from Whitestone and Starsilver, its point always wrapped in a bone-piercing chill. Its text tells how the outlander warrior Imunlaukr hurled this astral-silver lance to protect a maiden of Sal Vindagnyr, and the blow that legend names dolorous destroyed three kingdoms and killed her. Released in Version 6.6.

Lore: In the moonless city of snow, an outlander warrior mourned a shattered realm and left his old greatsword to the frost.

Owners: Imunlaukr is the warrior of the text; the wiki's Hexerei Series page states that the polearm once belonged to him.

key: Sharpness That Ceased Upon Wondrous Creation
Moment That Ceased Upon Waking From Grand Dreams
Pendulum That Ceased Amidst a Great Fall
62.content:
Disenchantment in Deep Shadow (also: Iridescence That Ceased Amidst Glory, Sharpness That Ceased Upon Wondrous Creation, Moment That Ceased Upon Waking From Grand Dreams, Ovations That Ceased Upon Festivity, Pendulum That Ceased Amidst a Great Fall): Disenchantment in Deep Shadow is a 4- and 5-star artifact set for Superconduct and Stellar-Conduct teams, released in version 6.6. Its five pieces are all about Aksinya, the silver-haired human scholar of the old Snezhnayan court: her friendship with a frost-wielding fae princess, her work among the ruins of the Shadow Realm, a long-haired alchemist who joined her research, and the Tsar who found her as an infant.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: 2-piece gives +18% ATK; the 4-piece boosts Superconduct and Stellar-Conduct reaction damage and CRIT Rate.

63.content:
Divine Bridle: The Divine Bridle is a bridle-shaped quest item from Enkanomiya (Byakuyakoku). It was the badge of the Sunchild's office, the sign that a child was the nation's puppet ruler. It has no power of its own. The spirit Aberaku hid it and gave it to the Traveler; the Traveler then used it to help the official Clymene release the souls of the seven Sunchildren.

Lore: Byakuyakoku was ruled by a Sunchild, an infant chosen to be the nation's figurehead and said to be a child of the sun. Per the quest accounts, the real power lay with people behind the scenes. The bridle marked the office. Aberaku, who built the Dainichi Mikoshi, calls it proof that a child is a child of the sun, and says he hid it intending to alert the people. Clymene, the official who raised the Sunchildren, believed it lost.

64.content:
Dodoco Tales: Dodoco Tales is a 4-star catalyst, a small children's book of cheerful adventure stories about the Dodoco, furry creatures from the Golden Apple Archipelago. Its text is told in a child's voice and says the book was given by the freest mother in the world to the luckiest daughter in the world. It was an event reward from Midsummer Island Adventure (Version 1.6), a limited-time event.

Lore: The tale says there is a group of islands in a foggy sea called the Golden Apple Archipelago, where the cute, peace-loving Dodo Clan live without troubles. They call each other "Dodoco", which means "the best of friends".

Owners: No owner is named in the text. The book is described as given by a mother to a daughter.

65.content:
Dragon's Bane: Dragon's Bane is a 4-star polearm of the Kunwu series, described as a polearm with an entwining golden dragon, light and sharp, that may well kill dragons with ease. It is rumoured to be a legendary polearm of Liyue. It has been in the game since Version 1.0.

Lore: It is called a legendary Liyue polearm that pierces anything in its way.

66.content:
Dragonspine Spear: Dragonspine Spear is a 4-star polearm of the Dragonspine series, in-game description "a spear created from the fang of a dragon" that is oddly warm to the touch. It is made from teeth of the shadow dragon Durin and is the reward of the world quest The Festering Fang. Added in Version 1.2.

Lore: The text narrates a very long dream. He dreamed that he and everyone had journeyed to a land of green grass and soulful songs, where he sang with the gentle people and danced in the skies with a dragon as beautiful as a jewel.

67.content:
Dream-Mirror Remnant (also: Skirk's Abyss Crystal): The Dream-Mirror Remnant is an Abyss Crystal that Skirk gave the Traveler, received at the end of the quest Unbounded in Version 5.7. When worn, it can be used during sleep to "dream-mirror" with her; using it again lets the holder revisit certain scenes from what happened during that case.

Lore: Skirk, Surtalogi's disciple, is an outsider who visits Teyvat to grow stronger. In Whispers Betwixt Stars and Night she offers to dream-mirror with the Traveler and Paimon so she can experience the Traveler's stolen-soul dream herself. Later, while the Traveler sleeps, they wander through Skirk's inner world and see her memories.

68.content: Dull Golden Bridle (also: Dull Golden Bridle of Byakuyakoku): The Dull Golden Bridle is a quest item found in Enkanomiya's library ruin during the world quest The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent. Its description calls it the hereditary national treasure of Byakuyakoku, drained of all power.

69.content:
Echoes of an Offering (also: Soulscent Bloom, Jade Leaf, Symbol of Felicitation, Chalice of the Font, Flowing Rings): Echoes of an Offering is a 4- and 5-star artifact set that rewards Normal Attacks. Its five pieces (Soulscent Bloom, Jade Leaf, Symbol of Felicitation, Chalice of the Font, Flowing Rings) carry item text made of Chenyu Vale legends: tea served when the spiritscent flowers bloom at Qiaoying Village, the first tea tree, a jade split into hidden pieces, and the friendship of the vale's adepti.

Lore: The pieces tell Chenyu Vale legends about its adepti, its tea and a sacred jade that was broken up and hidden.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: the 2-piece bonus raises ATK; the 4-piece bonus can add a bonus Normal Attack damage hit called Valley Rite.

70.content:
Electro Gnosis (also: Inazuma's Gnosis, Ei's Gnosis, Gnosis of the Electro Archon, Electro Archon's Gnosis): The Electro Gnosis is the Gnosis of Inazuma's Electro Archon: a small object shaped like a chess piece that connects an Archon to Celestia. Ei, the Raiden Shogun, gave it up and entrusted it to Yae Miko. Yae traded it to the Fatui Harbinger the Balladeer (Scaramouche) to save the Traveler. In Sumeru, Nahida took it from him, then gave it to the Harbinger Dottore. As of 7.1 it is one of the six Gnoses held by the Tsaritsa.

Lore: A Gnosis grants and strengthens elemental power and links its holder to Celestia; Nahida calls the Gnoses symbols of the Heavenly Principles' control over Teyvat and its "laws." Archons keep their thrones and their power without one: Ei is still the Electro Archon after giving hers away.

Owners: Ei (Raiden Shogun) -> Yae Miko -> the Balladeer (Scaramouche, later the Wanderer) -> Nahida -> Dottore -> the Tsaritsa (Anastasya).

71.content: Elegy for the End (also: The Parting Refrain, Millennial Movement: Farewell Song): Elegy for the End is a five-star bow released in version 1.4, one of the Millennial Movement weapons, each of which carries a song of Mondstadt's history. Its story tells of the Cataclysm, when a venomous dragon crushed the land, and of a dour knight who could be made to forget his duty only by a girl's song. He fell in the battle; she came home to find the song changed.

key: Emblem of Severed Fate artifact set
72.content:
Emblem of Severed Fate (also: Emblem of Severed Fate artifact set, Magnificent Tsuba, Sundered Feather, Storm Cage, Scarlet Vessel, Ornate Kabuto): Emblem of Severed Fate is a 4 and 5 star Inazuma artifact set. Its five item texts tell, in fragments, of the half-oni swordsman Iwakura Michihiro, also called Douin, and of the black-winged tengu Teruyo of Yougou who gave him his new name and fought him in thirteen yearly duels. Mechanically it rewards Energy Recharge with Elemental Burst damage.

Lore: The texts follow Michihiro, the son of an oni mother who lost her standing with the Shogun. After his family's fall he lived in seclusion; a black-winged tengu, Teruyo of Yougou, renamed him "Iwakura" (a seat of rock) to free him from the burden of oni blood and challenged him to yearly duels.

73.content:
Engulfing Lightning (also: Kusanagi no Inabikari, Ei's naginata, the Shogun's naginata): Engulfing Lightning is the polearm (a naginata) of Ei, the Electro Archon who rules Inazuma through her puppet, the Raiden Shogun. Its item text calls it a lethal weapon for cutting away "scattered dross" and speaks of Ei's vow to prune mortal obsession and unchecked desire in order to keep an unchanging, eternal world. Its Japanese name means roughly "grass-cutting lightning".

Lore: The weapon's story is told as Ei's reflection. From high above the storm clouds she looked on the mortal world she loved and saw petty disputes and fleeting obsessions that, to her, were enemies of eternity. Like weeds among crops, they had to be swept away by lightning, so that nothing needed to wither or be lost.

Owners: Ei is the wielder the text names. The Raiden Shogun, her puppet, fights with the same style of polearm.

74.content:
Envoy's Medal (also: Envoy's Medal of the Tsaritsa, Tsaritsa's special envoy medal): The Envoy's Medal is a medal the Tsaritsa gave the Traveler at Zapolyarny Palace in Version 7.1. It is proof that the Traveler is her special envoy, officially titled "Consultant to the Tsaritsa", and it gives unrestricted access to Zapolyarny Palace.

Status as of 7.1: The Traveler holds the medal as of Version 7.1.

75.content:
Etherlight Spindlelute (also: Last Singer): Etherlight Spindlelute is a 4-star catalyst: a lute whose golden strings shine like sunlight, which appears to be a relic from the Seelie of old.

Lore: Beyond the ruins of an ancient palace, at the edge of the Nod-Krai wasteland, stands the quiet sacred forest of Lake Amsvartnir. Legend says that whoever breaks the golden branch in the forest will find the royal court of the Seelie, hidden from mortal eyes by day.

Owners: No owner is named. The Seelie are its implied makers or keepers, and the court's owner is described as long departed.

76.content:
Everlasting Moonglow (also: Fumetsu no Gekka, Byakuya Kougetsu, Pearl and waves catalyst): Everlasting Moonglow is a pearl-strung catalyst from the Sangonomiya and Watatsumi tradition. Its item text is a poetic history of Watatsumi Island: the people who dreamed with their god, the first Divine Priestess, the lightning that struck down their dream, and the memory that survives in the "pearl and waves" emblem.

Lore: The text begins with the "pearl and waves" emblem of the Sangonomiya, said to mean the waves that embrace Watatsumi and its bright pearls, though some say it shows the jewelled wheel of Watatsumi Omikami keeping eternal watch over the coral land like the moon. It then recalls how the descendants of their god passed hope from generation to generation.

Owners: No wielder is named in canon. The weapon is tied to the Sangonomiya clan only by the emblem its text is built around.

77.content:
Exaiphanes Blade: The Exaiphanes Blade is a 5-star sword given to the Traveler during the Snezhnaya Archon Quest (Chapter VII, Act I), described as a longsword that once shone with the light of the stars and in the voyager's hand becomes a new light unconnected to any past era. It reacts to Statues of The Seven in Snezhnaya and can only be strengthened at them. Added in Version 7.0.

Lore: The blade is obtained in a special domain during Great Deeds on the Tundra, and it seems to react whenever the Traveler comes near a Statue of The Seven in Snezhnaya.

Owners: The blade is the player's Traveler's weapon, obtained during the Snezhnaya Archon Quest. Its Traveler's Path passive applies only when the Traveler equips it.

78.content:
Eye of Graeae (also: Graeae, Eye of Graeae gadget): The Eye of Graeae is a palm-sized mechanism that often takes the form of a monocle. The Traveler finds it in an abandoned train in Snezhnaya, where it wakes, recognises them as a Descender, and agrees to serve them. In Snezhnaya it lets its user shape Prime Ice, protects against the killing cold by burning Kresnik Energy, calls a train, and speaks as a polite, forgetful voice that is trying to recover its lost power.

Lore: The Eye was left in an abandoned train in Snezhnaya, untouched through the cataclysm. When it wakes, its memories are broken and its power is scattered across the tundra. It senses the pieces in three places and asks the Traveler for help, as the one it has "signed a contract to serve".

79.content:
Fables de Fontaine (also: Fables of Fontaine, Fontaine Animal Fables): Fables de Fontaine is a three-volume storybook of animal fables found in Fontaine, credited to the author Marie Hericart de La Fontaine. Each volume holds one short tale ending in a stated moral. Its in-game description says most of the tales were not originally written by her but gathered from ancient poems now lost.

Lore: Vol. 1, "The Maiden and the Sun": a fox's adopted daughter, grown to marriageable age, asks to wed the most powerful being in the world. The fox offers her to the sun, but the sun points to the clouds that block it. The clouds point to the wind, the wind to the mountain that stops it, the mountain to a mouse that can tunnel through it, and so on through the cat, dog and wolf. The chain returns to the sun, and the maiden marries the sun. The moral is that one should accept one's destiny and cannot escape a duty by excuses.

80.content:
Fang of the Mountain King (also: Turquoise Hunt, Kongamato's fang): Fang of the Mountain King is a 5-star claymore, a giant sword forged from pure turquoise. It is named for Kongamato, the Mountain King, because it is far heavier than ordinary weapons.

Lore: In the heart of Huitztlan sleeps Kongamato, the Mountain King, a creature as vast as the mountains around it. In its half-waking, searing pain it treats everything that approaches as a mortal enemy and attacks without distinction.

Owners: No wielder is named. The sword is named after Kongamato rather than owned by anyone.

81.content:
Favonius Codex: Favonius Codex is a 4-star catalyst, a secret tome that belonged to the scholars of the Knights of Favonius. It records the logic and power of elements and matter and is inlaid with crystallized elements. Every copy is hand-made, and its text is partly about the order's great library.

Lore: The book holds the collective knowledge of the Knights' scholars. Its crystals are precious both in themselves and because each codex is made by hand; the text says only scholars who truly understand the workings of the elements can make such crystals.

Owners: No owner is named. The text says it belonged to the scholars of the Knights of Favonius.

82.content:
Favonius Greatsword: Favonius Greatsword is a 4-star claymore of the Favonius series, a heavy ceremonial sword of the Knights of Favonius. It channels elemental power easily and is highly destructive, and its text tells of the Lion of Light Arundolyn and his childhood friend Rostam the Wolf Pup.

Lore: The text calls it an honor given to a Knight of Favonius and the fruit of the work and skills of Mondstadt's craftsmen, who achieved results in elemental affinity by studying the city's ancient artifacts. It reminds the bearer that destruction is only a means; the end is to defend what must be defended.

Owners: No owner is named in the text.

83.content:
Favonius Lance: Favonius Lance is a 4-star polearm of the Favonius series, a spear of honor among the Knights of Favonius. It is used in parades and reviews yet is also a keen foe of monsters. Its text recounts how spears came to Mondstadt and how the noble Eberhart took one up.

Lore: The text calls it a crystallization of the work and artistry of Mondstadt's defenders. By studying the arbor that held firm in the wind, the city's craftsmen and scholars learned much about elemental affinities. In hand, it reminds the Knights to be disciplined and to defend Mondstadt's freedom.

Owners: No owner is named in the text.

84.content:
Favonius Sword: Favonius Sword is a 4-star sword of the Favonius series, the standard-issue longsword of the Knights of Favonius. Its text credits Favonius Bladework to Rostam the Wolf Pup, childhood friend of Arundolyn, the Lion of Light, and says Rostam's skill has never been matched.

Lore: Mondstadt's craftsmen studied Mondstadt's Anemo to reach elemental affinity, and the sword is both an honor to a knight and the fruit of the defenders' skill. The text warns that its sharp blade is for defending, not attacking.

Owners: No owner is named in the text.

85.content:
Favonius Warbow: Favonius Warbow is a 4-star bow of the Favonius series, a recurve bow issued only to the Knights of Favonius' best, long-serving archers. Its text tells of the Outriders, the Knights' archer scouts, and how the team declined after their first member left.

Lore: The bow is a reward for worthy guardians of Mondstadt and a tool for their continued guardianship. The text says the Knights once had a formidable team of archer scouts called the Outriders, founded by a mercenary leader from Liyue who passed on a lifetime of knowledge.

Owners: No owner is named in the text.

86.content: Festering Desire (also: Undying Admiration, Durin's sword): Festering Desire is a creepy straight sword that almost seems to yearn for life, dripping with a shrivelling venom that could corrupt even a mighty dragon. Its blade was coated with powder made of the dragon Durin's remains. The Traveler received it as a memento from Albedo after the 1.2 event The Chalk Prince and the Dragon, once the corruption had been drawn out.

87.content: Finale of the Deep: Finale of the Deep is a four-star sword of the Beaumont series, made by forging in Fontaine. Its description calls the longsword as silent as the ocean depths and older than its styling suggests. The item story says it once belonged to a musician whose name is forgotten, a proud figure of Remuria's golden era whose doctrine of music as authority ended in catastrophe.

88.content:
Finale of the Deep Galleries (also: Deep Gallery's Echoing Song, Deep Gallery's Distant Pact, Deep Gallery's Moment of Oblivion, Deep Gallery's Bestowed Banquet, Deep Gallery's Lost Crown): Finale of the Deep Galleries is a 4- and 5-star Cryo artifact set. Its five Deep Gallery pieces carry item text about Skirk, following her master Surtalogi's guidance, walking the frozen north to find relics, with each piece telling part of a legend of the first angel, a stranger from beyond the stars and the Golden City's fall. Mechanically it rewards a character at zero Energy.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: the 2-piece bonus gives +15% Cryo DMG; the 4-piece bonus boosts Normal Attack and Burst damage at 0 Energy.

89.content:
Flame-Forged Insight (also: Mind in Bloom): Flame-Forged Insight is a 4-star claymore from Natlan. The People of the Springs are said to have forged a great blade to protect a child who would go on a distant journey, and this weapon is a replica of that legendary sword.

Lore: Akamai and Kau Kau, two youths of the People of the Springs, once swore to explore all of Natlan and see their deeds recorded on woven scrolls. Their treasures turned out to be mostly ordinary ore and crystals, but they treasured them anyway.

Owners: No owner is named. The wiki calls this particular weapon a replica of the legendary sword.

90.content: Fleuve Cendre Ferryman (also: the Ferryman): Fleuve Cendre Ferryman is a four-star sword from Fontaine that is, plainly, a handy length of abandoned copper pipe once used as a weapon, famous or infamous depending on the circle. Its item story belongs to Eduardo Baker, an outlaw leader of the Fleuve Cendre, who called it the Ferryman for the many who went into the grey river with it. It is obtained from the Fontaine Fishing Association rather than forged.

91.content:
Flower of Paradise Lost (also: Ay-Khanoum's Myriad, Wilting Feast, A Moment Congealed, Secret-Keeper's Magic Bottle, Amethyst Crown): Flower of Paradise Lost is a Sumeru desert artifact set (Version 3.3, City of Gold domain) about the Lord of Flowers, also known as Nabu Malikata, goddess of the oasis and mother of the Jinn. Its texts tell how she was cast aside by the heavens, how the Jinn were born from her wanderings, and how she bent to her friend King Deshret's ambition at a heavy price.

Lore: Long ago the heavens cast out the Lord of Flowers. She wandered the barren desert for seventy-two nights; her wounds became springs, the springs became gardens, and night-blue water lilies sprouted. The Jinn were born from those lilies. The first Jinn begged her to stay and she remained, and purple moon-like flowers named Padisarah bloomed wherever she walked.

92.content:
Flower-Wreathed Feathers (also: Inflorescence Unattainable): Flower-Wreathed Feathers is a 4-star longbow from Natlan that burns like a flame, adorned with feathers said to come from the ancient tyrant Ngoubou. It belongs to the Heroes of Natlan series.

Lore: A dying old sage tells the hero Menilek, "bearing the name Transcendence", that a calamity older than his name flows in the veins of the injured Saurian whelp in his arms, and that if he pities mortals he should sever its neck and give it freedom. Menilek ignores the oracle and tends the whelp.

Owners: The feathers are tied to Ngoubou; the bow itself is tied to Menilek by the legend.

93.content: Flowing Purity (also: Clockwork Coppelia): Flowing Purity is a four-star catalyst of the Beaumont series, forged in Fontaine. The weapon is a strangely shaped anthology said to record all the scripts written by Coppelius, and the item text presents a reconstruction of fragments from his last opera, Clockwork Coppelia.

94.content:
Flute of Ezpitzal (also: Ezpitzal, priestly flute): The Flute of Ezpitzal is a 4-star sword from Natlan: a peculiarly shaped jade longsword that the Masters of the Night-Wind have passed down as a "priestly flute". Its story explains how the tribe called Mictlan began.

Lore: Long ago, when dragons still roamed a deep valley, a girl with mutilated ankles inherited the title of Holy Sovereign. Dragons, frightened into withdrawing into dreams, had made a pact with the mortals: they would shield the village with a labyrinth of mirrors and a fortress of mist if the people chose a Sovereign to guide them into their dreams.

Owners: Handed down among the Masters of the Night-Wind. Its story is tied to the Holy Sovereign and to Maghan.

95.content:
Forest Regalia: Forest Regalia is a 4-star claymore of the Aranara series. The description says it has taken the shape of a greatsword that shall cut down the foes of the forest. Its story tells, through an Aranara's memory, of the last king of the forest and the shifting maze of his palace.

Lore: The tale begins "The forest used to be a giant maze many, many moons ago..." The last king of the forest has returned to Sarva, leaving one who once waited upon him to inherit the name "Tiger". Where there was shade, there was the forest king's domain, and birds and beasts bowed as he passed.

Owners: No owner is named, and no character is recorded wielding it.

96.content: Forged by the Golden Melody: Forged by the Golden Melody is a four-star claymore added in Version 7.0 through the Battle Pass Gnostic Hymn. The description calls it a greatsword decorated in gold and says legend holds it was the favored weapon of an exalted Harmost of the distant past. Its story is a conversation in the white-stone halls of Remuria between a musician and his golden-haired friend.

97.content:
Fractured Halo (also: Purifying Crown, Electrifying Edict): A spinning mechanical blade produced by the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop, seeming to hide secrets from a bygone era. A 5-star polearm from Version 5.8, wielded by Ineffa.

Lore: After her revival, Ineffa remembers an age even bards forget, but her memories feel hollow, like thoughts flaring and fading in a trance.

Owners: Ineffa wields it; the text says Aino forged it for her.

key: The Grand Jape of the Turning of Fate
98.content:
Fragment of Harmonic Whimsy (also: Harmonious Symphony Prelude, Ancient Sea's Nocturnal Musing, The Grand Jape of the Turning of Fate, Ichor Shower Rhapsody, Whimsical Dance of the Withered): Fragment of Harmonic Whimsy is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from Fontaine, added in Version 4.6. Its five pieces are written as one story: Remus, a god who lost his homeland, becomes the God King of Remuria, is told that his glorious empire will drown, and chooses to fight fate with a "Grand Symphony." The set is a Remurian legend, not a family heirloom.

Lore: The set tells a Remurian legend in order. A homeless god from the desert, later called Remus, meets a prophet, becomes king over the High Sea, hears that his realm will fall, and gambles on a symphony to break fate.

99.content: Freedom-Sworn (also: Revolutionary Chorale, Millennial Movement: Song of Resistance): Freedom-Sworn is a five-star sword released in version 1.6, a Millennial Movement weapon whose story is a Mondstadt resistance song. The song says that if someone takes your tongue you can still sing with your eyes, and that stealing your song and your freedom "shall never do". It was sung through Decarabian's reign and the aristocracy's, and when five rebels climbed Decarabian's tower.

100.content:
Frostbearer: Frostbearer is a 4-star catalyst of the Dragonspine series. Its in-game description is "a fruit that possesses a strange, frosty will," with a faint sense of agony. It is the one weapon of the series obtained only by forging, using a diagram from the Frostbearing Tree. Added in Version 1.2.

Lore: When the daughter of the priest of Vindagnyr was born beneath the white tree, the verdant mountain kingdom rejoiced at her blessing. Those who wrote the kingdom's annals believed that Sal Vindagnyr's blessing, like the undying silver-white tree, would last forever.

101.content: Frostbreath (also: Frostbreath polearm, A Cast Real Far): Frostbreath is a four-star polearm in the Gnostic Hymn 3 series, added in version 7.0 as a Battle Pass weapon. Its in-game description calls it a spear of solid ice imbued with a chill, said to have belonged to the Belyi Tsar who ruled Snezhnaya long ago. Its story follows the young Monomakh, trained by his master, who asked whether stronger spears exist.

102.content:
Fruitful Hook (also: The Weight of Falling Branches): Fruitful Hook is a 4-star claymore from Natlan: a hooked blade made by the courier-hero Burkina of the Scions of the Canopy, with the hero Tenoch's help, to harvest the finest Flamegranates from the great mother tree.

Lore: A young courier, Burkina, was royally annoyed at a Saurian living on the mountain's other side who mocked his movements, so he swore to climb to the peak and harvest the Flamegranates of the mother tree to show off to the most agile Yumkasaurus of all.

Owners: Made by Burkina with Tenoch's help. No later wielder is named.

103.content:
Funerary Mask (also: Signora's mask, mask of La Signora): The Funerary Mask is a quest item the Traveler receives after defeating La Signora, Eighth of the Fatui Harbingers, in a duel before the Raiden Shogun's throne in Tenshukaku, Inazuma (Version 2.1). Its text calls it a trophy and uses it to reflect on why Fatui wear masks.

Status as of 7.1: The Traveler holds it as of Version 7.1; nothing read says otherwise.

104.content:
General History of Snezhnaya (also: General History of Snezhnaya (I), General History of Snezhnaya (II)): General History of Snezhnaya is a two-volume book sold by Moes at Torchlight Books in Snezhnograd (added in 7.0). Written by Y. S. Klyucheva and dedicated in fawning terms to Tsaritsa Anastasya, it is Snezhnaya's flattering "official" history: legends of golden Hyperborea, then the youth and campaigns of Tsar Monomakh (the Belyi Tsar) and his fae companions.

Lore: Volume 1 sets out rival legends of Hyperborea, a warm golden realm where Snezhnaya now lies. Volume 2 tells how young Monomakh learned the spear from Yalyane Morevna, beat the shapeshifter Filipov and made him his "Synaimos" (sworn comrade), and spared the human warrior Nepla Korolevitsna's clan.

105.content:
Geo Gnosis (also: Morax's Gnosis, Gnosis of Morax, Geo Archon's Gnosis, Rex Lapis's Gnosis): The Geo Gnosis was the Gnosis of Morax, the Geo Archon, who now lives in Liyue as Zhongli. A Gnosis is a gleaming, chess-piece-like focus that an Archon carries in their chest. Zhongli gave his to the Fatui Harbinger Signora in Liyue Harbor (1.1), fulfilling a secret contract with the Tsaritsa that he called his "contract to end all contracts".

Owners: Morax (Zhongli), then Signora, then the Tsaritsa (Anastasya), who holds it as of 7.1.

106.content: Gest of the Mighty Wolf (also: Indomitable Chivalry, Four Winds' Hymn): Gest of the Mighty Wolf is a five-star claymore of the Hexerei series, released in version 6.4. Its description says it was forged by Ravenwood, who inherited the name of Boreas, before he became a knight. The item story is a Mondstadt tale of a nameless northern knight and his wolf companion Andrius, and of the blacksmith's son who admired him.

107.content:
Gilded Dreams (also: Dreaming Steelbloom, Feather of Judgment, The Sunken Years, Honeyed Final Feast, Shadow of the Sand King): Gilded Dreams is a Sumeru desert artifact set (Version 3.0, Spire of Solitary Enlightenment domain). Its five pieces remember a lost golden age: a desert paradise ruled by a "God King" who judged every heart, three inseparable friends, and a law that hardened into chains. The set never names the God King; other lore points to King Deshret.

Lore: Ancient legends tell of three inseparable friends: one withered like a rose in the mud, one made a great hidden oasis, one used all their intellect to build an eternal illusion in the sand. They meant for no one to suffer partings or bitter water, and promised a "golden slumber".

108.content:
Gladiator's Finale (also: Gladiator's Nostalgia, Gladiator's Destiny, Gladiator's Longing, Gladiator's Intoxication, Gladiator's Triumphus): Gladiator's Finale is an ATK artifact set (4 and 5 star, 1.0) about the champion gladiator of aristocracy-era Mondstadt, a slave who nearly won his freedom, was undone by pride and a master's flattery, and fell to a young girl in the arena. The girl is Vennessa, the later founder of the Knights of Favonius. Its weapon companion is the polearm Deathmatch.

Lore: A slave gladiator rose to legend in the arena. His master flattered him into staying, and a girl defeated him in his last bout.

109.content: Glaze Lily (also: Glaze Lilies, Liuli Baihe): The Glaze Lily is a very old flower of Liyue, once common across the land and now rare in the wild. Its item text says it turns the land's memories into scent as it blooms. Legend says it opens to pure, beautiful music, and that someone once loved it above all other flowers.

110.content: Golden Frostbound Oath (also: Dawn's Salutation Returned): Golden Frostbound Oath is a five-star bow released in version 6.5 (Luna VI). Its in-game description calls it a longbow carved from ancient whitewood, once wielded by the Jack Frost King of the northern lands. Its story follows the Knight of the Golden Bough, who walks into the frozen north seeking the Golden Bough to save fallen Arcadia and finds the sacred tree already ruined.

111.content:
Golden Troupe (also: Golden Song's Variation, Golden Bird's Shedding, Golden Era's Prelude, Golden Night's Bustle, Golden Troupe's Reward, Golden Troupe artifact set): Golden Troupe is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from Fontaine, added in Version 4.0. Its five pieces tell the story of Boethius: a boy from a conquered island tribe who became a musician and Harmost of Remuria, and, after the empire's fall, the troupe that clung to the dream of its golden age. Its bonuses boost Elemental Skill damage.

Lore: The pieces follow the rise and ruin of the Remurian golden order through the musician-Harmost Boethius and end in the troupe that waits for the symphony to play again.

112.content:
Great Song of Khvarena (also: Great Songs of Khvarena, Great Khvarena): The Great Songs of Khvarena are five large concentrations of Khvarena, the purifying power left by the divine bird Simurgh. The Pari elder Zurvan says she fused them long ago to cleanse the land of impurity. They hold immense power, but only a Pari who has earned the Khvarena's approval can unleash it, through a special ritual. In Vourukasha Oasis's quest series, Sorush the Pari and the Traveler gather all five, and Nasejuna, leader of the Order of Skeptics, is revealed to have been using them for his own plot.

Lore: Zurvan says that after she scattered the monsters that invaded the sea of flowers, she fused the strongest Khvarena gathered into five Great Songs to purify the land. She hid one in Sunyata Lake for a time of need, and the rest were scattered. A Pari needs the Twin-Horned Chaplet, the symbol of the Khvarena's recognition, to touch them. Sorush earns it by being acknowledged as a Bloomguard.

113.content:
Hakushin Ring (also: Hakushin no Wa, Ring of Kitsune Saiguu): The Hakushin Ring is a catalyst that carries the memory of the Kitsune Saiguu, a kitsune of the ancient Hakushin clan who lived in Narukami's mountains and walked among humans. Its short description admits that the device is "but an impoverished vessel" for the full breadth of her thought. Its text is her fond recollection of the friends she made and a final plea.

Lore: The speaker is the Hakushin Kitsune. She calls her life "simple and ordinary" and says she has lived it to the full, running with her agile and loveable comrades across the mountains and plains of Narukami. She hopes they will be able to run happily again once everything is over.

Owners: The Kitsune Saiguu, the Hakushin of the text, is the originating figure; the physical ring is a memory-bearing device rather than a known heirloom.

114.content: Hamayumi (also: the shrine maiden's warbow, evil-banishing bow): Hamayumi is a four-star bow of the Amethyst series. Its text is told from a Seirai shrine maiden's point of view: she watches the bandit Ako Domeki (called Zaemon) refuse to bring her aboard the Seiraimaru, thinks of her late archery teacher, and secretly decides to use "true magic" learned on Mt. Yougou against the Electro Archon's ships. The name nods to the real hama yumi, a sacred evil-banishing bow carried by shrine maidens.

115.content:
Haran Geppaku Futsu (also: Haran, Rippling Upheaval, Geppaku Futsu blade): Haran Geppaku Futsu is a celebrated sword of the Futsu school of smiths in Inazuma. It is the only surviving blade forged by the great smith Masagomaru (Futsu Masayoshi). Its name pairs "Haran", meaning turmoil or roiling waves, with the Geppaku Futsu series, of which it is the "Rippling Upheaval" blade.

Lore: Two Geppaku Futsu swords were made. Hasui was forged by Futsu Minori, third-generation head of the school; its pale blue blade and water-like hamon were often seen at the waist of the Shogun's valet. It was later broken in a mortal duel to decide the fate of the oni people and sent back for reforging.

Owners: Futsu Masayoshi (Masagomaru) is the smith, not an owner. No wielder is named in the item text.

116.content:
Heart of Depth (also: Ocean Conqueror, Gilded Corsage, Gust of Nostalgia, Copper Compass, Goblet of Thundering Deep, Wine-Stained Tricorne): Heart of Depth is a Hydro artifact set (4 and 5 star, added 1.2), also called Ocean Conqueror in the Adventurer Handbook. Its pieces show the last voyage of the Skipper's Chief Mate: a sardonic, hard-drinking exile from a gray aristocratic land, who joined a Liyue sea captain's hunt for the monster that haunted them both. The wiki names him as Parsifal.

Lore: The Chief Mate was no native of Liyue but came from a gray land ruled by an aristocracy, rumoured to have disgraced his house. He drank to forget, followed the Skipper to sea, and met his end in the vengeful hunt for a giant sea creature.

117.content:
Heart of the Furnace (also: Foundryman's Conjecture, Foundryman's Observation, Foundryman's Calculus, Foundryman's Magnanimity, Foundryman's Legacy): Heart of the Furnace is a 4- and 5-star artifact set for Stellar Glimmer teams, released in version 7.0. Its five pieces, all titled "Foundryman's...", tell the story of a young Domovoy from Kitezhgrad: his rise at the furnace core, his secret assignment, his apprenticeship under the human scholar Aksinya and his later power as president of the Royal Energy Commission.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: 2-piece gives +18% ATK; the 4-piece boosts ATK and the party's Stellar Glimmer reaction damage.

118.content:
Heretic's Molten Blade (also: Lone Light's Blessing, Och-Kan's blade): Heretic's Molten Blade is a 4-star sword from the Battle Pass, belonging to Och-Kan, the Sacred Lord of Ochkanatlan. A gift from the red-haired Pyro Archon, it was later turned against him.

Lore: Och-Kan stood alone in his empty royal hall and drew a sword that had gone unused for so long its edge had dulled. He kept it spotless for decades, though he was no swordsman.

Owners: Och-Kan, the Sacred Lord, is the owner. He received the blade from the red-haired Pyro Archon and died by it.

119.content:
Hilichurl Cultural Customs (also: Hilifolk Study): Hilichurl Cultural Customs is a four-volume study by Jacob Musk, a Mondstadt ecologist whom the books call the 'Poet Laureate of Hilichurlian'. It records how hilichurl tribes organise themselves, what they revere and how three tribes of Dadaupa Gorge differ. It is a field scholar's account, often condescending and incomplete.

Lore: Vol. 1 (social structure): hilichurl tribes are small and treated like a large family. The oldest member, the shaman, usually leads, wears a horned smiling mask and chants; but in some tribes a larger, stronger hilichurl with a horned mask takes over, which makes the tribe more aggressive. Resources seem to be shared according to need. Vol. 2 (spirituality): they worship elemental power itself rather than an Archon, and masks and body paint show a member's element. Vol. 3: the huge solitary Lawa are called 'king' but do not lead. Vol. 4: the Meaty, Sleeper and Eclipse tribes of Dadaupa Gorge show cultural diversity.

key: The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria
History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria
120.comment: The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria
120.content:
The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria (also: History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria, Decline and Fall of Remuria, Pulteney's history of Remuria): The History of the Decline and Fall of Remuria is a three-volume book of Fontaine, said to be the work of the great scholar Pulteney, written in the early years of Fontaine's founding. It tells how King Remus raised the empire of Remuria, how it was destroyed, and how Egeria afterwards brought order to the tribes. Each volume ends on the saying that oceans will rise, empires will fall, and the only constant is change.

Lore: Vol. 1 opens with the legend that the ocean gave birth to everything and also devoured it. Heaven drowned the early peoples for turning from their fate, and the survivors lived like animals until the great king Remus descended on Meropis in his golden ship Fortuna, taught farming, built cities and temples, and spread music and art.

121.content: Holy Lyre der Himmel (also: Holy Lyre, Barbatos's lyre, Lyre of the Heavens): The Holy Lyre der Himmel is Mondstadt's sacred lyre, said to be the instrument Barbatos, the Anemo Archon, once played. The Church of Favonius keeps it. In the Prologue the Fatui hide it, the Traveler retrieves it, and Dvalin's purified tears restore enough of its power for Venti to use it against the Stormterror's madness.

122.content:
Hunter's Path: Hunter's Path is a 5-star bow of the Sumeru series, a golden hunting bow made of precious white branches. Its description says it has felled countless wicked beasts trying to infiltrate the woods. The story is about a huntress who pursued a dark herd so long that she forgot the human tongue and became a beast herself.
