Lore: A hunter pursues a dark herd in a hunt that never seems to end, waiting nights under rotten leaves and sleeping inside carcasses, always moving to the next target after the fatal arrow. She stops caring about the wind revealing her location or about camouflaging her scent with wildflowers, as her smell becomes like that of wild beasts. She forgot the human tongue before she became a hunter, and even the blind youth who first found her and gave her the white-branch bow was forgotten.

Owners: No owner is named. The huntress is the only wielder in the text.

key: Husk of Opulent Dreams artifact set
123.content:
Husk of Opulent Dreams (also: Husk of Opulent Dreams artifact set, Bloom Times, Plume of Luxury, Song of Life, Calabash of Awakening, Skeletal Hat): Husk of Opulent Dreams is a 4 and 5 star Inazuma artifact set that tells, in dream-like fragments, the life of a puppet made to hold a "heart": the figure once known as Scaramouche, Sixth of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers (the Balladeer), who now goes by the Wanderer. It is a defence and Geo-damage set.

Lore: The pieces read as snapshots of a wanderer: a vessel made for a heart and left to sleep, a gold ornament of the Shogun's, a young traveller turned away by a rain, and a name taken from the villains of Inazuma's theatre.

124.content:
Hydro Gnosis (also: Fontaine's Gnosis, Gnosis of the Hydro Archon, Hydro Archon's Gnosis): Fontaine's Gnosis, the chess-piece-like divine focus of the Hydro Archon. Focalors, the real Archon, hid inside the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale with it while Furina played the god in public for some 500 years. After Focalors's execution (4.2) it passed to Neuvillette, who gave it to the Harbinger Arlecchino as a "diplomatic gift".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is in Snezhnaya, one of the six Gnoses the Tsaritsa holds.

125.content:
Hymn of the Maelstrom: Hymn of the Maelstrom is a 5-star catalyst, an exquisite lamp of blue chalcedony that looks like a treasure from a fairy tale. It is said that a song of praise, forgotten by all, slumbers sealed inside. Its text is a fairy tale a storyteller tells a young Water Imp about a child born of the waves. Added in Version 7.1.

Lore: A young Water Imp who sings alone keeps close a fairy tale from her youth: a child born of the breaking waves, nobler than the daughters of the sea, whose voice made mariners sink into whirlpools and thawed frozen seas.

Owners: Canon names no owner. The text is about a Water Imp and her tale, not about a possessor.

key: Prayer Songs of the Frostmoon Scions
126.content:
Hymns of the Far North (also: Hymns of the Far North (I), Prayer Songs of the Frostmoon Scions): Hymns of the Far North is a three-volume book of prayer songs of the Frostmoon Scions, compiled by the priestess Ehrnrooth and found at the Frostmoon Enclave (added in 6.0). Most of its rites are long disused. Each old prayer is followed by Ehrnrooth's note on how the first Moonchanter, Aila, replaced it with a short prayer to the pale Frost Moon.

Lore: A priestess's collection of hymns to the old gods of the far north, each with a note explaining how and why the first Moonchanter simplified it. It reflects the Scions' faith before and after Aila.

127.content: Jadefall's Splendor (also: Jadefalls Splendor, Bìluò zhī Lóng): Jadefall's Splendor is a five-star catalyst and a ritual vessel carved from jade, reflecting the luster of the skies and clear waters. Its item story says jadeite fell from the sky, was washed clean and was shaped by mortal hands into a splendid instrument awaiting its sacred purpose. The rest of the text is a tea-table debate between a scholar from Sumeru and a consultant in dark robes about whether history bends toward decay or rebirth, framed by the story of Chenyu Vale's ancestors.

128.content:
Kagotsurube Isshin (also: Cursed Blade, Prized Isshin Blade (reforged), Kagotsurube): Kagotsurube Isshin is a long blood-red sword bearing the Isshin name. It was forged by Akame Kanenaga, an Inazuman smith of the fallen Akame school, but made in a snowbound land to the far north rather than in Inazuma, and its journey home was marked by dark deeds. It figures in Kaedehara Kazuha's Story Quest, where the possessed sword is finally reforged and the player receives it.

Lore: The text says people often think each blade holds a blade-spirit; a sword forged by the Tatarigami would then hold a demon of malice. Akame Kanenaga was a swordsmith who failed to become head smith. He made this blade in a snow-covered northern land, not in the land of thunder and Jade Steel.

Owners: Akame Kanenaga forged it. After the Story Quest, Kazuha holds the reforged sword.

129.content:
Kagura's Verity (also: Kagura no Shin'i, Yae Miko's kagura bells, Kagura bells): Kagura's Verity is the set of bells used for the Kagura Dance, blessed by Yae Miko, the Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine, and still carrying the scent of the Sacred Sakura. Its item text is Yae's voice, looking back on her long friendship with Ei and the people and spirits she has met across her life.

Lore: The text opens with the white silhouette of the past, which never returned and remains an unceasing dream. In Yae's recollection she was a silly little thing, nowhere near as clever as the great matriarch Hakushin. As a whelp foraging through snow she tried to catch Ei's attention; her foolhardy courage earned Ei's pity and she entered her service, warming her hands and feet, a "very great honor".

Owners: Yae Miko is the blesser and voice of the text. The bells are tied to the Guuji's duties at the Grand Narukami Shrine.

130.content:
Kamera (also: Kamera gadget, Kamera Gadgets, Fontainian Kamera): The Kamera is a photographic device that records a picture at the press of a button and prints it on paper. Canon calls it a special item from Fontaine. In Liyue the Feiyun Commerce Guild imports it as a novelty, and the Traveler receives one as thanks for a small errand.

Lore: Xu, a member of the Feiyun Commerce Guild at Liyue Harbor, says the Guild recently imported a new product from Fontaine, reportedly very popular there. You press a button and an image appears on a piece of paper. He enjoys it a great deal, and the Guild's young master is convinced it will sell well.

131.content: Katsuragikiri Nagamasa (also: Daitatara Nagamasa, Nagamasa's nagamaki): Katsuragikiri Nagamasa is a four-star claymore, a tough, simple nagamaki-style blade designed by Mikoshi Nagamasa, an inspector of Tatarasuna. It was originally named the Daitatara Nagamasa. After he used it to execute his own subordinate Katsuragi, the sword and its owner's title were renamed for that act.

132.content:
Key of Khaj-Nisut: The Key of Khaj-Nisut is a 5-star sword of the Deshret series. The in-game description calls it one of a paired set of scepters fashioned from obsidian, said to work as a key to the gate of a paradise at the end of the ocean of sand. Its story follows a hidden prince, later called Xiphos, and the aged blind poet who served and then freed him.

Lore: The story is set after the Lord of Sand's dreams fell apart and the Grandmaster of Verdure hid away the whispers of the demonic skies. A queen of one of the many kingdoms that arose from the broken realm burned her little prince's gilded robes and crown and sent him away in a servant's sackcloth. He grew up as the son of one who ruled the slave markets and then became a wanderer who had lost everything. His last master was a blind poet.

Owners: Named in the text: the prince Xiphos, who wields it as his key, and before him his master the blind poet. Legend adds mortal tyrants and kings in between.

133.content: Kitain Cross Spear (also: Kitain's cross spear, Kitain Bunsou's spear): Kitain Cross Spear is a four-star polearm: a strangely shaped, very heavy spear made by Kitain Bunsou for his own style of spearmanship. Item text says it is unwieldy for the untrained but destructive in expert hands. The Kitain family had long hunted the Tatarigami and served as the Prefects of Yashiori Island.

134.content:
La Chanson d'Erinnyes (also: Chanson d'Erinnyes, The Song of Erinnyes): La Chanson d'Erinnyes is a three-volume epic of Fontaine in the style of a knightly song, about the Lochknight Erinnyes, called the Knight of the Lakelight. It shows her refusing King Remus's demand for tribute, the knights rallying behind her, and her farewell to the Mistress of Many Waters, after which she throws her sword into the lake and vanishes.

Lore: Vol. 1: A musician sent by King Remus arrives at Aremori Castle during Erinnyes's victory feast and demands water and earth as tribute and submission to the Sumphonia Capitolii, the eternal harmony. Erinnyes forbids harm to him and answers that her people bend the knee only to the Mistress of Many Waters.

135.content:
Lavawalker (also: Lavawalker's Resolution, Lavawalker's Salvation, Lavawalker's Torment, Lavawalker's Epiphany, Lavawalker's Wisdom): Lavawalker is a Pyro-resistance artifact set (4 and 5 star, added 1.0). Its five pieces tell of the Lavawalker, a proud sage who wore a flame-flower brooch, a crimson agate circlet and a phoenix feather, walked onto the burning sea of the Mare Jivari and was never seen again. In Natlan, the Abyss Lector Enjou is linked to the name.

Lore: A sage called the Lavawalker defied the flames of the Mare Jivari. His teacher, jealous, sent him into the fire wearing the circlet; he strolled out over the lava and faded into the horizon.

136.content: Legend of the Lone Sword (also: Jin the Seventy-Second): Legend of the Lone Sword is a four-volume martial arts novel that sells well in Liyue Harbor. Its blurb stresses that the story takes place in a world without elemental energy or alchemy, so swordsmanship is purely physical skill and nerve.

137.content:
Light of Foliar Incision: Light of Foliar Incision is a 5-star sword of the Sumeru series, a gilded blade made from precious white branches. Its description says it was once used to destroy countless poisons that infested the forest. The story follows an exiled prince from the golden desert who is spared by a huntress in Dharma Forest and told to break off a pale branch.

Lore: A wanderer from the land of gold, once a prince, whose body and mind are scarred by battle, is lost in the green maze of the forest. The ancient forest king, tasting the scent of blood stemming from authority, sighs and summons a huntress with a moon-white bow to hunt the beast that has come from beyond the woods.

Owners: In the story, the exiled prince Faramarz is the one rumoured to have forged a blade from the pale branch; the wiki calls him its creator and wielder.

138.content: Lightbearing Moonshard (also: Legacy of Lang-Gan): Lightbearing Moonshard is a five-star sword added in Version 6.3 (Luna IV). Its description calls it a legendary blade forged from glimmering moonlight gathered in a well by an adeptus hidden among clear springs, its true form revealed only where dusk meets dawn. The item story is a Liyue legend about a girl of the mining tribes who seeks that adeptus and the sword that could save her people's ancient kingdom.

139.content:
Lion's Roar: Lion's Roar is a 4-star sword of the Kunwu series, a sharp blade with extravagant carvings that does not compromise on durability and sharpness and that roars like a lion as it cuts the air. It is rumoured to be a legendary sword of Liyue. It has been in the game since Version 1.0.

Lore: The blade is so sharp that its victims realise they have been struck only an hour later.

140.content:
Lithic Blade: Lithic Blade is a 4-star claymore of the Lithic series, a greatsword carved and chiselled from the very bedrock of Liyue. The Millelith of old favoured it, but it is so heavy that no ordinary human can lift it. It was added in Version 1.3.

Lore: It is made of the divine bedrock upon which Liyue Harbor was established, and it is incomparably heavy; records say the Millelith of old wielded it with ease.

141.content:
Lithic Spear: Lithic Spear is a 4-star polearm of the Lithic series, a spear forged from the rocks of the Guyun Stone Forest whose hardness knows no equal. It was favoured by the Millelith of old, and its great weight stops today's Millelith from equipping it. It was added in Version 1.3.

Lore: The Millelith conducted themselves in Rex Lapis' name by the axiom: while rock stays hard, the mountain shall never fail; while the Millelith stands guard, evil shall never prevail. In the past they went forth to subdue demons and protect roads and countryside; in peaceful times their duties have shifted to maintaining order.

142.content:
Long Night's Oath (also: Lightkeeper's Pledge, Nightingale's Tail Feather, A Horn Unwinded, Dyed Tassel): Long Night's Oath is a 4- and 5-star artifact set that rewards Plunging Attacks. Its five pieces (Lightkeeper's Pledge, Nightingale's Tail Feather, Undying One's Mourning Bell, A Horn Unwinded, Dyed Tassel) carry item text that reads as a folk history of Nod-Krai: how the Lightkeepers swore their oath, how the Wild Hunt and the Abyss threatened the borderlands, and how the oath was renewed again and again at great cost.

Lore: The five pieces tell Nod-Krai's story from its founding oath to the cost of keeping it, centring on the Lightkeepers who guard the region.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: the 2-piece bonus raises Plunging Attack DMG; the 4-piece bonus stacks a Plunging Attack damage buff.

key: Lost Prayer to the Sacred Winds
143.comment: Lost Prayer to the Sacred Winds
143.content:
Lost Prayer to the Sacred Winds: Lost Prayer to the Sacred Winds is a 5-star catalyst: an educational tome by anonymous early worshippers of the wind, blessed by the wind for its faithfulness over the millennia. Its text follows the scripture through Mondstadt's ages and ends with a farewell note from a believer who joins the thousand winds. Added in Version 1.0.

Lore: Under the Storm Lord, who reigned from his tower, the scriptures filled with desperate appeals. In the era when the sands of snow thawed, the joy of sprouting greenery flooded the pages.

144.content: Lumenstone (also: Lumenstone Adjuvant): Lumenstone is a special stone mined from the depths of The Chasm in Liyue. Its item text says it has catalytic properties and nearly blazes with light in the gloomy mines, but loses all such effects once taken out of the Chasm. Entering the Underground Mines requires an adjuvant made from it.

145.content:
Lumidouce Elegy (also: Bright Dawn Overture): Lumidouce Elegy is a 5-star polearm adorned with azure crystal. It is said to have been the treasure of a legendary Champion Duelist, yet never once used.

Lore: In the Fleuve Cendre undercity where there is neither rain nor sun, a girl scraped by for scraps and would kill for a slice of mouldy bread, accepting that the weak are prey. Her mother's teaching was ashes to ashes, dust to dust.

Owners: A legendary Champion Duelist, linked by the wiki to Marfisa. The weapon was never used.

146.content: Magical Crystal Chunk (also: Magical Crystal Chunks, Magical Crystal Ore): Magical Crystal Chunk is a blue crystal from mines whose rock was eroded by the energy of the Ley Lines. Ordinary methods cannot process it. Only Original Resin can refine it, into Mystic Enhancement Ore for strengthening weapons.

147.content:
Maiden Beloved (also: Maiden's Distant Love, Maiden's Heart-Stricken Infatuation, Maiden's Passing Youth, Maiden's Fleeting Leisure, Maiden's Fading Beauty): Maiden Beloved is a healing artifact set (4 and 5 star, added 1.0). Its pieces tell of a sheltered noblewoman rescued by a white knight, who fell in love with him and spent her years waiting for a man devoted to chivalry. She is the counterpart to the knight of the Bloodstained Chivalry set.

Lore: A maiden was saved by a white knight and gave her heart to him that day. He took only a white flower and went on his way; she waited for the rest of her life.

148.content:
Makhaira Aquamarine: Makhaira Aquamarine is a 4-star claymore of the Tulaytullah series: an ancient greatsword that gleams like water, whose unnaturally sharp edge a thousand years of sand erosion has not dulled. Its legend belongs to the dancer Makhaira, once a tyrant's concubine.

Lore: A thousand years ago, when the foolish king (Deshret) was buried beneath the dunes, short-lived city-states were scattered across the gilded land. The sword belonged to the dancer Makhaira, once the tyrant's concubine, who won the king's favor and the prince's attention with a ruthless sword dance.

Owners: The sword belongs to Makhaira in its story. No modern character is recorded wielding it.

149.content:
Marechaussee Hunter (also: Hunter's Brooch, Masterpiece's Overture, Moment of Judgment, Forgotten Vessel, Veteran's Visage, Marechaussee Hunter artifact set): Marechaussee Hunter is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from Fontaine, added in Version 4.0. Its pieces are mementos of the old Marechaussee Hunters, chiefly Emanuel Guillotin, who directed the Siege of Poisson, retired scarred and drinking, and raised two children he never felt close to. The bonuses boost Normal and Charged Attacks and CRIT Rate when HP changes.

Lore: The set tells, through objects, how the Marechaussee Hunters began, how one Hunter broke at Poisson, and how the people around him were changed by it.

150.content: Memory of Dust (also: the stone dumbbell, Mortal World's Lock): Memory of Dust is a five-star catalyst of the Liyue series, a stone puzzle dumbbell. Its item story recounts Morax remembering Guizhong, who gave him the dumbbell as a token and a challenge: all her wisdom is hidden inside, if he can unlock it. He never could.

151.content:
Mistsplitter Reforged (also: Kirigiri no Kaikou, Mistsplitter, Takamine's sword): Mistsplitter Reforged is a sword from Inazuma's past, one of the blades the Shogun bestowed on her Hatamoto. It was carried by the samurai Takamine the Mistsplitter, who used it against demons and Tatarigami, and who fought the dark army of the Cataclysm at the end of his life. The sword broke and was reforged from its fragments, so the "Reforged" in the name marks it as a successor bearing the old name.

Lore: The text says the sword was shattered into a thousand pieces and reforged. Its user, Takamine the Mistsplitter, appears in a children's rhyme listing famous martial artists, after Arataki of the Front Gate, Iwakura the Successor and Kitain the Serpent.

Owners: Takamine the Mistsplitter is the only named user. The Shogun is named as the one who gave such swords to her Hatamoto.

152.content:
Mitternachts Waltz: Mitternachts Waltz is a 4-star bow described as painted in the color of transgression and nights of illusion. Its text is a dramatic, German-flavored tale: the Prinzessin der Verurteilung and her Night-Severing Raven, Ozvaldo Hrafnavins, recount a long journey across space and time. The wiki notes Fischl is shown with this bow in her TCG card.

Lore: The tale opens with Oz telling the Prinzessin that not one of her tears was shed in vain on her pilgrimage. The Prinzessin and her raven, in their journey across space and time, witnessed countless stories and their endings.

Owners: No owner is named in the text. The wiki notes Fischl is seen wielding this bow in her TCG character card.

153.content: Moonfall Silver (also: Moonfall Silver crystal): Moonfall Silver is a silver crystal as pure and pristine as moonlight, a local specialty of Nod-Krai. Canon says it has almost perfect elemental affinity, which is why Nod-Krai craftspeople treat it as an excellent elemental conductor. It is found on Hiisi Island.

154.content:
Moongazer's Engraving (also: Moongazer Engraving, Stellar Blackbody message): A two-volume set of stone tablets on the Frost Moon (6.7) recording the Stellar Blackbody's message: a warning that pitch-black annihilation crosses the universe, and a plea to keep a light burning.

Lore: The message warns, gently, of pitch-black annihilation crossing the universe and says the listener is not alone.

155.content:
Moonweaver's Dawn (also: Secret Silver's Testament): An immaculate silver sword that slices armour like moonlight through an empty night; legend says it was blessed by the first Moonchanter, Aila. A 4-star sword of the Frostmoon Scion series from Version 6.0.

Lore: A guardian addresses her ward Aila as her heart's child and tells her the pure silver blood of their line alone is worthy of the Frost Moon's grace.

Owners: No wielder is named; the blade is attributed to Aila's blessing.

156.content: Mora (also: Mora coins, Mora currency): Mora is the common currency of Teyvat, accepted in every nation. It takes its name from Morax, the Geo Archon, whom Liyue calls Rex Lapis. All of it is minted at the Golden House in Liyue. Loading-screen text calls it the one language everybody speaks.

157.content: Mouun's Moon (also: Mouun's longbow, the Watatsumi shrine maiden's bow): Mouun's Moon is a four-star bow of the Watatsumi series, the longbow of the Watatsumi shrine maiden Mouun. Item text says it shines pure white like seafoam at the tip of a moonlit wave. She befriended the monsters of the distant seas and fought with them against the thundering clouds in the war of Orobashi (Watatsumi Omikami), a path of no return that ended in tragic obliteration.

158.content:
Musou Isshin (also: Musou no Isshin, Makoto's blade, the Shogun's sword): Musou Isshin is the legendary sword of the Raiden twins. It was created from Makoto's divine might and kept unsharpened and unused while she lived, as a symbol of true peace. When Makoto died in the Cataclysm it passed to her sister Ei, who began to use it in battle. It is the blade the Raiden Shogun draws from her heart during her Elemental Burst.

Lore: The character story calls it a sword that has accompanied Ei to this day and has "witnessed both time and eternity". It was born from Makoto's divine might but never sharpened, because Makoto was not one for battle; it was a symbol, a sign of true peace.

Owners: First Makoto, who never used it to fight, then Ei, who has used it in battle since Makoto's death. The Raiden Shogun, Ei's puppet, wields it in her Burst.

key: New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune
Urakusai's Chronicles of the Six Kitsune
159.comment: New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune
159.content:
New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune (also: Chronicles of the Six Kitsune, Urakusai's Chronicles of the Six Kitsune, Black Fox Itaru): New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune is a six-volume Inazuman novel sold at the Yae Publishing House in Inazuma City. It adapts "Urakusai's Chronicles of the Six Kitsune", a hit about 500 years ago, and follows the tales of Itaru, eldest of the six apprentices of the Great Kitsune Hakushin. Its last volume adds the author's commentary on the Kitsune Saiguu and why she left.

Lore: The Prologue frames the book. An aging writer meets Yae Miko at the Uyuu Restaurant and is persuaded to write again; she notes she was not yet born when "she" (the Kitsune Saiguu) left, and that he is the only one still able to recite the stories she told.

key: Night Murmurs From the Far Border
Night Murmurs From the Far Border: Varcolac
160.comment: Night Murmurs From the Far Border
160.content:
Night Murmurs From the Far Border (also: Night Murmurs From the Far Border: Varcolac, Varcolac folktale): A one-volume book of Snezhnayan fae folktales, sold in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai (6.3). Its story follows a hunter who tracks a wounded wolf-like monster to a remote mansion and learns that its lord is a Varcolac, a fae with two hearts.

Lore: The hunter Czcibor shoots a huge black-furred beast in the shoulder, follows its blood trail to a mansion and finds a young lord with long black hair. He discovers the lord is the beast, kills him, and learns that a Varcolac has two hearts and does not die from one.

161.content:
Night of the Sky's Unveiling (also: Bloom of the Mind's Desire, Feather of Indelible Sin, Revelation's Toll, Vessel of Plenty, Crown of the Befallen): Night of the Sky's Unveiling is a 4- and 5-star artifact set added in version 6.0 that strengthens Lunar reactions. Its item text tells of Rauthvangi, a young stargazer of subterranean Khaenri'ah who glimpsed a "pitch-black Elysium" beyond the sky. For this he was exiled, survived the surface, wandered the nations, and as Rotwang, the Tsar's "mad monk", travelled to Nod-Krai to claim a hidden treasure and break out of the celestial shell.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: a 2-piece Elemental Mastery bonus and a 4-piece bonus that rewards Lunar reactions with CRIT Rate and shared Lunar reaction damage.

key: Nighttime Whispers in the Echoing Woods
162.comment: Nighttime Whispers in the Echoing Woods
162.content:
Nighttime Whispers in the Echoing Woods (also: Selfless Floral Accessory, Honest Quill, Faithful Hourglass, Magnanimous Ink Bottle, Compassionate Ladies' Hat): Nighttime Whispers in the Echoing Woods is a Geo artifact set from Version 4.3. Its five pieces tell a bedtime-style fairy tale, read aloud in fragments by a little girl in an attic with her dog Pie: a witch in the Echoing Woods grants a youth's wish, and the girl he loves is given endless good luck that turns out to be a curse.

Lore: A girl follows her dog Pie into the attic and finds a storybook with golden-winged butterflies on its cover. It says a witch in the Echoing Woods grants any wish but hides her hut in fog and echoes, so few reach her. A youth, led by a golden-winged butterfly, finds the hut and asks that the girl he loves, who loves another, have all the happiness in the world. The witch agrees; the price will come later and need not be his soul.

163.content:
Nightweaver's Looking Glass (also: Looking Glass of the Nightweaver, Millennial Hymn): A flawless silver mirror said to have witnessed the Moon Maiden's birth; the Frostmoon Scions hold it a relic of unrivalled provenance. A 5-star catalyst from Version 6.0.

Lore: Its story opens with a prophecy-verse: the Eternal Moon fell, the Iridescent Moon shattered, the Frost Moon ceased to turn, and the world marches toward its end until Elysium dawns.

Owners: No wielder is named in canon; the description ties the mirror to the Frostmoon Scions as a whole.

164.content:
Noblesse Oblige (also: Royal Flora, Royal Plume, Royal Pocket Watch, Royal Silver Urn, Royal Masque): Noblesse Oblige is a 4- and 5-star artifact set (1.0) about the old aristocracy of Mondstadt: nobles who began as heroes and guides of the people and decayed into idle, grasping rulers. Its name is French for 'nobility obliges'. It drops in the Clear Pool and Mountain Cavern domain.

Lore: The nobles of old Mondstadt were examples to the people, noble in conduct as well as birth. Later nobles let indulgence and power ruin them.

165.content: Noctilucous Jade (also: Night-Staying Stone, Yepo Stone): Noctilucous Jade is a rare mineral from Liyue that glimmers in the dark. Its item text says it is a mutated gemstone condensed from the world's flourishing elements. It is found in caves and mines across Liyue, especially near Mingyun Village.

166.content:
Nocturne's Curtain Call (also: Ballad of the Crossroads, Bountiful Sea's Sacred Wine): A jade pearl wrapped in moonlight whose gentle warmth lingers like a song even on the coldest winter night. A 5-star catalyst from Version 6.3, its text a lullaby and a vision of the Moon Maiden.

Lore: The text is framed by a lullaby to a little dove, child of the moon: may the moon be with you in your slumber. Between its verses is Columbina's vision of the Moon Maiden drifting through the night.

Owners: No wielder is named; the text concerns Columbina but does not make her the owner.

167.content:
Nymph's Dream (also: Odyssean Flower, Wicked Mage's Plumule, Nymph's Constancy, Heroes' Tea Party, Fell Dragon's Monocle, Nymphs Dream): Nymph's Dream is a 4- and 5-star artifact set that boosts Hydro damage and ATK. It was released in Version 3.6, long before Fontaine opened, and its lore tells a quiet story: orphans playing heroes, wicked mages and fell dragons, a tea party that pauses the adventure, and the later scattering of the "Narzissen champions" after a catastrophe.

Lore: Told as children's play and reminiscence, the set follows the Narzissen champions from their games to their separation after a disaster.

168.content:
Oathsworn Eye (also: Oath Eye, serpent's eye jewel): Oathsworn Eye is a jewel-like catalyst that glimmers like a snake's eye. Its description calls it a national treasure of Byakuyakoku, stored in the Dainichi Mikoshi, and says that when the Serpent God came, it was used to notarize great oaths and wishes. Its item text is a short fable of the oath a lonely serpent swore with a child and with his people in the depths.

Lore: The text imagines the giant white snake looking down at a child who asks him to become their deity. The snake says he fled into waters unknown because he could best neither Deus Auri nor Narukami, and warns that anyone who keeps seeking the light will suffer loss. Yet he shows a snake-eyed jewel and says: swear it upon this eye, as he did when he made a pact with his coral servants.

Owners: No individual is named. The eye belongs to Byakuyakoku as a national treasure, and its home was the Dainichi Mikoshi.

169.content:
Obsidian Codex (also: Obsidian Codex artifact set, Reckoning of the Xenogenic, Root of the Spirit-Marrow, Myths of the Night Realm, Pre-Banquet of the Contenders, Crown of the Saints): Obsidian Codex is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from Natlan, added in Version 5.0. Its five pieces are mythic fragments, each opening with the line that many stories "were never recorded or eulogized in any human history": a dragon's gift of fire to humans, the first tribe, a contest of heroes and the crowning of a king who ended the tribes' wars. It boosts characters in Nightsoul's Blessing.

Lore: The set tells, from several angles, how the old dragon civilization faded, how humans received fire and organised into tribes, and how a hero without a prophecy united them.

170.content:
Ocean-Hued Clam (also: Ocean-Hued Clam artifact set, Sea-Dyed Blossom, Deep Palace's Plume, Cowry of Parting, Pearl Cage, Crown of Watatsumi, Sea-Dyed Foam): Ocean-Hued Clam is a 4 and 5 star artifact set from Watatsumi Island's songs. Its texts recall Omikami, the sea god the islanders worshipped; the first Divine Priestess and her twin sisters; shells and pearls given as tokens of family; and the sacrifice that ended that age. It is a healing set whose 4-piece turns healing into burst damage.

Lore: Watatsumi's people say they came out of the dark depths, and took a single shell each as a keepsake of their clan; those who had none were welcomed into another family. Omikami chose a Divine Priestess and rulers from among them, and the age ended in sacrifice.

171.content:
Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale (also: Oratrice, Oratrice Mecanique, Mechanical Oratress of Cardinal Analysis): The Oratrice is a huge mechanical scale in the Opera Epiclese, Fontaine's court-theatre. At trials it weighed the arguments, returned the verdict the Iudex had to honour, and turned judgment into Indemnitium, the energy that powered the Court of Fontaine. Fontaine believed it was Furina's creation; in truth Focalors, the real Hydro Archon, built it and hid inside it. In 4.2 it sentenced "the Hydro Archon" to death and executed Focalors. It has not functioned since.

Status as of 7.1: Since Focalors's execution (4.2) the Oratrice no longer works. Neuvillette hears cases and passes verdicts himself.

172.content: Padisarah (also: Padisarahs, Padisarah flower): The Padisarah is a holy, noble flower of Sumeru. It is very demanding about where it grows, and its buds are processed into valuable spices. Its archive text says it is a cultivar restored to the land by the Anahitian Blessing, after the original flower vanished.

173.content:
Pale Flame (also: Stainless Bloom, Wise Doctor's Pinion, Moment of Cessation, Surpassing Cup, Mocking Mask): Pale Flame is a 4- and 5-star artifact set added in version 1.5. Its five pieces read like origin stories of the Fatui: the first Fatuus (Pierro) approaches a woman consumed by fire, a heretical scholar, a moneyman and a discarded constructed being, and each takes a role in the Tsaritsa's cause. The last piece, the Mocking Mask, is Pierro's own declaration. In it he says the blood of his Khaenri'ahn compatriots cannot be washed away and that he will become a jester who mocks fate.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: the 2-piece bonus is +25% Physical DMG; the 4-piece bonus boosts ATK after Elemental Skill hits.

174.content:
Parametric Transformer (also: Parametric Transformer gadget, transmutation device): The Parametric Transformer is a gadget the Traveler wins in Liyue by solving an Adventurers' Guild treasure riddle. It is a mysterious device from the ruins that can "transmute" material objects: a heap of ordinary materials goes in, and different materials come out after elemental energy has charged it.

Lore: Lan, who works at the Liyue Harbor Adventurers' Guild, posts a rumour about treasure near Tianqiu Valley. Nobody has found it. The Traveler follows a treasure map to Dunyu Ruins, reads a rhyming note about a giant tree, a road and a flight of stairs, opens three chests, and finds a strange box. Lan has never seen anything like it.

175.content:
Peak Patrol Song (also: Halcyon Years Unending, Ode to Flowers): Peak Patrol Song is a 5-star sword: an obsidian blade of unparalleled sharpness and light as a song, modified by an artisan (linked to Xilonen) with a detachable Phlogiston device that plays records.

Lore: Every year, before the Embercore Flowers bloom, the mistress of the mountain mines comes alone to Tequemecan Valley to lay dew-kissed flowers for friends who never saw the dawn. Her once-hard heart has softened with age.

Owners: No wielder is named. The description's only person is the artisan who modified the blade, linked to Xilonen.

key: Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon
176.comment: Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon
176.content:
Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon (also: Clustered Storage Array): The Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon is a flawless piece of jade, the heart of the Dragonlord Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon Ch'ule-L (nicknamed Ixlel), who ruled Chichen Uctokah, the original city of Ochkanatlan, before human civilisation was kindled. The Traveler receives it at the end of the Natlan World Quest "Open Your Heart to Me". Its energy is exhausted, so it can no longer command anything.

Lore: The item text says the heart once let its owner command every device in Ochkanatlan, "the ineffable city". It is now spent. The text also remarks that, like the half-humans who chased it, the Dragonlord's quest for perfection ended in something as cold and lifeless as jade.

177.content:
Perinheri (also: Hleobranto Innamorato): Perinheri is a two-volume Fontaine book, also called 'Hleobranto Innamorato', a legend said to come from Khaenri'ah. It follows the knight Perinheri, his friend and rival Hleobrant, and Angelica, a wandering woman who claims to be a princess.

Lore: In an age when a crimson moon shone over the underground kingdom, an orphanage raised foundlings to be knights. Perinheri, one of its best, and Hleobrant fall out over Angelica, a woman who will marry only the strongest knight; beyond the kingdom's borders Hleobrant is revealed cursed, and Angelica reveals herself as freedom.

178.content:
Polestar Ballet Anthology (also: Black Snow Swan, The Seabird, The Envoy, The Firebird): A four-volume set of Korolevskiy Troupe ballet scripts from Snezhnaya (7.0). Vol. 1 is Black Snow Swan, about a black swan who refuses to give up love to become pure; Vols. 2 to 4 hold The Seabird, The Envoy and The Firebird.

Lore: Vol. 1, Black Snow Swan: the dark-feathered swan Odile is told by Queen Myrtha that love is a poison. Three spirits show her love's cost, but she chooses love and flight. Vol. 2, The Seabird: the composer Kostya loses Zarechnaya and himself. Vol. 3, The Envoy: a town panics at a rumoured imperial inspector and is fooled by a thief. Vol. 4, The Firebird: a prince, the Firebird and a captive princess defeat a demon king.

179.content: Primogem (also: Primogems): Primogems are the premium currency of Genshin Impact. Their item text calls them a primordial crystalline gem beyond the mundane world, shining with the condensed hopes and dreams of universes that once were. In play they are spent mainly on wishes.

180.content: Primordial Jade Cutter (also: Primordial Jade sword, Pányán Jiélǜ): Primordial Jade Cutter is a five-star sword of Liyue, a ceremonial blade masterfully carved from pure jade. Item text says that when Liyue first arose, Rex Lapis once walked the land with a sword hewn from jade. It was cut as a costly gift for peace and luxury, then bathed in blood in war. It is a legend rather than a quest object: no scene shows the sword.

181.content: Primordial Jade Winged-Spear (also: Primordial Jade Winged Spear, Hépú Yuān): Primordial Jade Winged-Spear is a five-star polearm of Liyue. Its item story is a creation legend: at Liyue's foundation a sea behemoth called Baqiu, which the Geo Archon's own Geo Whale could not beat, drowned settlements with its waves. The Geo Archon hand-forged a black kite from jade and stone, it dove into the sea, and Baqiu sank for good.

key: Princess Mina of the Fallen Nation
182.comment: Princess Mina of the Fallen Nation
182.content:
Princess Mina of the Fallen Nation (also: Mina of the Fallen Nation): Princess Mina of the Fallen Nation is a six-volume Inazuman adventure novel series, sold by Kuroda at the Yae Publishing House in Inazuma City. A wandering samurai in luxurious robes, accompanied by a small girl in an oversized haori, takes a princess prophesied to bring destruction on a journey to the Sky Tower at the centre of the world. The blurbs sell it as a hugely popular romantic adventure.

Lore: Vol. 1: after thirteen years of peace, a century-scale age of warring states begins; a wandering samurai and a girl stop at a checkpoint where the samurai quickly disposes of three ashigaru. Vol. 2: the princess asks what the samurai thinks about her prophesied destruction; he calls the prophecy an excuse for war. Vol. 3: they see the devastation the war has caused. Vol. 4: a flashback. Vol. 5: at the Sky Tower the onmyouji reveal their plan. Vol. 6: the samurai walks the desert and leaves for another world.

183.content: Prized Isshin Blade (also: Accursed Isshin blade, the cursed Isshin sword): The Prized Isshin Blade is a four-star sword that exists only inside Kaedehara Kazuha's Acer Palmatum Chapter, Act I ("A Strange and Friendless Road", Version 2.8). It is a blade full of Tatarigami malice that possesses a samurai and goes hunting for Kazuha, wanting to prove that the Isshin Art can beat even the Shogun. Kazuha defeats it, the curse drains out of it, and at the end of the quest it is remade into the ordinary, obtainable Kagotsurube Isshin.

184.content:
Prototype Archaic (also: Prototype Gǔhuá): Prototype Archaic is a forgeable 4-star claymore of the Prototype series. Its description calls it an ancient greatsword discovered in Blackcliff Forge that swings with such force it seems to cut through reality. It has been in the game since Version 1.0.

Lore: It is an ancient prototype greatsword from Liyue's arsenal. The batch number has faded and no records confirm the date of production.

185.content:
Pyro Gnosis (also: Natlan's Gnosis, Gnosis of the Pyro Archon, Pyro Archon's Gnosis): The Pyro Gnosis is the Gnosis of Natlan's Pyro Archon, Mavuika, and the only one of the seven the Fatui never obtained. Capitano fought Mavuika for it and failed. In 6.6 she gave it away so Nahida could burn the corrupted Irminsul, and it vanished in the fire. As of 7.1 nobody knows where it is.

Status as of 7.1: Missing as of 7.1; the only Gnosis the Tsaritsa lacks.

key: Astral Whispers Beyond the Sacred Throne
186.content:
Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow (also: Rain Bow, Astral Whispers Beyond the Sacred Throne): Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow is a 4-star bow, an ancient ceremonial weapon passed down by the Masters of the Night-Wind, dark and forever wreathed in an unshakable chill. Its story tells of a covenant between a young priest and a rainbow-winged dragon.

Lore: Cinder City and its usurper's dream collapsed in a blaze when the scarlet-eyed hero called down the god's fiery wrath and burned the corrupt throne to ash. Decades earlier Maghan the dragon slayer had driven the old ruler from the deep valleys.

Owners: Used by Maghan in the story; carried into the Night Realm by Wagadu. No modern bearer is named.

key: Records of Hanan Pacha book collection
187.content:
Records of Hanan Pacha (also: Records of Hanan Pacha book collection): Records of Hanan Pacha is a three-volume collection of Natlan folk tales about the Sage of the Stolen Flame, Waxaklahun Ubah Kan. Vol. 1 tells how he and a companion, Chaac, tricked a vain winged dragon and took the power of phlogiston. Vol. 2 tells how they raised the land of Hanan Pacha and taught people to use it. Vol. 3 tells how the people broke a taboo and were driven out. The game itself labels it a fable with no basis in historical fact.

Lore: Told in the age of dragons, when the Lord of the Night ruled the night realm and no Pyro Archon yet existed. Humans had no Visions and were at the mercy of the elements until the Sage brought phlogiston from the "red and black land".

188.content:
Records of Jueyun (also: Jueyun Records): Records of Jueyun is a six-volume book collection of folk stories, myths and legends of Liyue by an author named Wuyuan. Each volume handles one tale: living stone beasts, a Sea God who takes brides, the haunted ruins of Wuwang Hill, the lonely seelie of the mountains, the gentle qilin, and the ancient Dunyu Ruins. The in-game blurb calls it quite a page turner.

Lore: - Vol. 1, Stone Beasts: Liyue's animal statues are said to wake on cool autumn nights and wander. Qingce elders say they are illuminated beasts who fought beside Rex Lapis in the Archon War and asked him to turn their mortal flesh to lasting stone.
- Vol. 2, Palace Beneath the Sea: a Sea God collects a village bride each festival in return for calm seas. One bride is released, keeps his sea-snail shell, and years later blows it when her own daughter is to be given up; the village is drowned.
- Vol. 3, Wuwang: Wuwang Hill, north of Mt. Qingce, is haunted by spirits that lure travellers off the path.
- Vol. 4, Mountain Spirits: seelie are held to be good omens that guide travellers and Vision-bearers to treasure.
- Vol. 5, Qilin: gentle illuminated beasts of the mountains who sometimes take human form and live among mortals.
- Vol. 6, Hidden Jade: the Dunyu Ruins, north of Nantianmen and northwest of Liyue Harbor, were a walled city whose people sealed it and left.

key: Mighty Redhorn Stoic Stonethreshing Gilded Goldcrushing Lion Lord
189.content: Redhorn Stonethresher (also: Redhorn Pestle, Mighty Redhorn Stoic Stonethreshing Gilded Goldcrushing Lion Lord): Redhorn Stonethresher is a five-star claymore whose item story is a folk tale. Its full name is the "Mighty Redhorn Stoic Stonethreshing Gilded Goldcrushing Lion Lord", and it was the beloved blade of an eccentric known as the "Otogi Kongou Lion King". Because both names were too long, the village children called the weapon the Redhorn Pestle and its wielder the Otogi King.

190.content:
Reed Miller's Cognoscenti Keepsakes (also: Proof of the Cognoscenti, Proofs of the Cognoscenti, Cognoscenti keepsakes, Memorata-Cognoscenti's Jest, Inscripta-Cognoscenti's Feather, Devocina-Cognoscenti's Sorrow, Weavenexa-Cognoscenti's Intoxication, Stratagema-Cognoscenti's Mask): The Proofs of the Cognoscenti are five quest-item relics in Nod-Krai, each "said to be a keepsake from Reed Miller", founder of the Treasure Hoarders: a silver mask, a black feather, a stopped timepiece, a goblet and a rusted flower. Legend says they point to his Great Treasure. The Traveler collects all five in East of the Moon, West of the Sun.

Lore: Folk retellings of the master thief, mixing legend and rumour, not eyewitness history.

191.content:
Reliquary of Truth: Reliquary of Truth is a 5-star catalyst added in Version 6.1. The in-game description calls it an angular box carved from gold and jade that legend says was once enshrined in a temple deep within Tulaytullah, the Sapphire City. Its story is about a young noble named Goudarz, who is given a power by a holy sage in exchange for an honest answer, and who rises as the king Saleb Dowleh, a king whose reign is built on lies.

Lore: After the great tower of Shah Ramshahr fell, the royal power passed among states as fleeting as dew. The nobles of Tulaytullah, free of the tyrant, followed false sages into new carnage. By the time the brutal Khagans arrived on horseback, no warriors guarded the Garden of Endless Pillars, and foreign soldiers and tax collectors preyed on the weary people. People then looked back to the brief reign of King Humayun.

Owners: No owner is named. Goudarz, later King Saleb Dowleh, receives the Staff of Falsehoods in the story; the reliquary itself is only said to have been enshrined in a temple of Tulaytullah.

192.content:
Retracing Bolide (also: Summer Night's Bloom, Summer Night's Finale, Summer Night's Moment, Summer Night's Waterballoon, Summer Night's Mask): Retracing Bolide is an Inazuma artifact set from launch (Domain of Guyun). Its five "Summer Night's" pieces record, in a man's voice, meetings with a fox-eyed woman at summer festivals near Mt. Yougou: lost as a child, nursing a sprained ankle as a teenager, and as an adult hoping to see her again. The wiki links her to Kitsune Saiguu.

Lore: At a summer festival a lost child, separated from his parents by the crowd carrying the divine palanquin, cries by the torii gates on the road to the shrine. A beautiful woman with fox-like eyes takes his hand and offers to see fireworks, throw darts and play fusen. Years later, on a festival night, the same woman sits beside him on a rock by the wayside, unchanged after ten years, and invites him to watch the fireworks with wine.

193.content:
Revelations of Divine Love: A book of poetry, a quest item, given by Hannelore, a Church of Favonius nun at Dornman Port. It is said to be by an ancient Church priest guided by the Anemo Archon.

Lore: The description presents it as a work from the ancient Church of Favonius that ends by treating all human love as sacred, because it comes from a longing for freedom.

194.content:
Rex Incognito (also: Rex Incognito novel): Rex Incognito is a four-volume Liyue fantasy novel telling of Rex Lapis' incognito excursions among mortals. A framing story set in the antique shop Xigu Antiques, run by Min'gui, surrounds tales of a jade craftsman and a harsh fishing-boat owner. Its running theme is that rules matter less than a person's own judgement, and that a relic is worth its story.

Lore: - Vol. 1: At night, Xigu Antiques of Feiyun Slope is visited by a black-robed young man who calls a damaged jade plaque in her shop a modern counterfeit. He argues that ancient tribes of Rex Lapis' followers carved such plaques as stand-in currency before Mora existed. The owner, Min'gui, says she can disprove his verdict with a story.
- Vol. 2: A prankish jade carver in Mingyun Village is asked by an amber-eyed woman to carve the true likeness of the Lord of Geo from what he has seen, or go unpaid. He delivers a plaque showing a woman and explains his three-day process of learning, observing and carving by heart.
- Vol. 3: A harsh fishing-boat owner in Liyue Harbor docks the pay of a new hand, a bashful youth from Qingce Village, who tells him a story about a jade plaque while someone takes the docked wages from the owner's pocket and returns them to the labourers.
- Vol. 4: Back in the shop, Min'gui argues that antiques are valued for their stories. The young noble buys the plaque, and admits his jade-currency theory was invented.

195.content:
Rhinedottir's "Gift" (also: Rhinedottir's Gift, Rhinedottir's "Gift" quest item): Rhinedottir's "Gift" is a quest item from the world quest Old Friends and New Knowledge (Version 6.2). It is the present that Rhinedottir sent to her creation Albedo through her cat Sebas, and it carries a short riddle about a tree, its perfect fruit and a seed of dreams. Albedo's only response is that he needs to think.

Lore: Albedo's master Rhinedottir sends the gift via Sebas, her old cat-butler, together with a spoken message. The message says that once a problem is solved, dwelling on it loses its point, and urges Albedo to pose questions of his own instead of resting on answers. The gift's text then compares a tree proud of its most perfect fruit with a "seed of dreams" that refuses to be only the king of a universe confined to its flesh.

196.content:
Ring of Yaxche (also: Yaxche Ring, Echoes of the Plentiful Land): Ring of Yaxche is a 4-star catalyst you forge: a jade vessel made by a hero of yesteryear, said to have shot down the giant dragon of the volcano. Its story belongs to the twin heroes Ahpub and Ixquieh.

Lore: In the age of myth, when great dragons roamed Natlan, the lost twin heroes reunited before an evil dragon's corpse and swore, upon sacred Yaxche, to end death, destruction and pain, and to ensure the strong never again bully the weak.

Owners: No wielder is named. The ring is a jade vessel attributed to the heroes of the legend.

197.content:
Royal Bow: Royal Bow is a 4-star bow of the Royal series, an old royal longbow of the erstwhile rulers of Mondstadt. Countless generations later its string is still tight and fires with great force. Its text is about the fall of the ruling Lawrence Clan and the Knights of Favonius exiling them.

Lore: Hunting was once a pastime of the nobles. They showed their strength in the natural world and shared the spoils with the people in benevolence. Benevolence was lost, and with it their reign.

Owners: No owner is named; the text says only a noble who ruled Mondstadt.

198.content:
Royal Greatsword: Royal Greatsword is a 4-star claymore of the Royal series, an old greatsword once used by the nobles who ruled Mondstadt, made of the finest materials and described as a weapon for royals only. Its text covers the noble duty to fight monsters and the history of gladiatorial combat.

Lore: Combat was once a responsibility of the nobles, who protected their people from monsters. They all but forgot that duty, which turned them into the very monsters they once sought to destroy.

Owners: No owner is named; the text says only that nobles used such greatswords.

199.content: Royal Grimoire (also: royal mage's grimoire): The Royal Grimoire is a four-star catalyst of the Royal series. It is a wax-treated scroll that once belonged to a royal mage of Mondstadt, holding both historical accounts and spells. Its item story is mainly a bitter note on how the nobility and their mage tutors failed Mondstadt, and on an oath whose wording was lost.

200.content: Royal Longsword (also: longsword of the old nobles): The Royal Longsword is a four-star sword of the Royal series. It was the sword of a noble who ruled Mondstadt, made of premium materials and still as sharp as ever. Its item story laments that noble swordsmanship, once meant to refine wisdom and elegance, decayed into formality, and recalls an oath of protection sworn 2,600 years ago.

201.content: Royal Spear (also: noble's hunting spear): The Royal Spear is a four-star polearm of the Royal series. It was kept in the collection of a Mondstadt noble, remains as sharp as the day it was forged, and in the aristocracy's own time never left the dark. Its story contrasts noble sword-fighting with the spear as a commoner's weapon.

202.content:
Sacrificer's Staff (also: Untainted Desire, Archpriestess's staff): A silver-white polearm, pure and without blemish, which legend says the Archpriestesses of Hyperborea used to guide their flock of Frostmoon Scions. A 4-star polearm of the Frostmoon Scion series from Version 6.1.

Lore: A fading Archpriestess hands the staff to her kind adopted daughter Lovia, telling her only her mercy can open the eyes of the lost.

Owners: The text passes the staff to Lovia, the last Archpriestess; no current wielder is named.

203.content:
Sacrificial Bow: Sacrificial Bow is a 4-star bow of the Sacrificial series, in the game since Version 1.0. Its item text calls it a ceremonial hunting bow petrified by time, once the property of the proud Lawrence clan of old Mondstadt, who used it in ritual reenactments of their victory over the frozen wilderness.

Lore: The Lawrence clan used the bow to act out their ancestors' conquest of the frozen wilderness in sacrificial ceremonies, and the bow itself was said to tell the story of the pioneers and their hardships.

204.content:
Sacrificial Fragments: Sacrificial Fragments is a 4-star catalyst in the Sacrificial series from Mondstadt. Its description calls it a weathered script whose text is no longer legible, a cursed item eroded by the winds of time. Present since Version 1.0.

Lore: Early Mondstadt built theaters atop windy cliffs and performed rituals as stories and ballads, because they believed the gods enjoyed stories.

Owners: No owner or clan is named in the item text.

205.content:
Sacrificial Greatsword: Sacrificial Greatsword is a 4-star claymore of the Sacrificial series, in the game since Version 1.0. Its item text describes a ceremonial greatsword that began as a prop and was hardened by time, once belonging to the Imunlaukr clan, brave and gifted warriors who fought hard and died young.

Lore: The Imunlaukr clan used it in sacrificial ceremonies to enact duels between brave warriors stained black with blood.

206.content:
Sacrificial Sword: Sacrificial Sword is a 4-star sword of the Sacrificial series, in the game since Version 1.0. Its item text describes a ceremonial sword, originally a prop and sharpened by time, that belonged to the kindly Gunnhildr clan, who enacted the defense of Mondstadt in rituals for the winds of time.

Lore: The Gunnhildr clan used it in sacrificial ceremonies that enacted the defense of Mondstadt.

207.content: Sakura Bloom (also: Sakura Blooms, Hiou-kyuu): Sakura Bloom is a petal that has fallen from the Sacred Sakura of the Grand Narukami Shrine, and a local specialty of Inazuma found on Narukami Island. Electro energy keeps the petals floating in mid-air.

key: Chalice of Your Blood and Sorrow
208.content:
Scarlet Proof (also: Honor to Your Devotion, Glory to Your Legacy, Time Gifted Unto You, Chalice of Your Blood and Sorrow, Testament to Your Faith): Scarlet Proof is a 4- and 5-star artifact set for Stellar Swirl teams, released in version 7.0. Its five pieces are bright red Fatui keepsakes (a flower medal, a quill, a pocket watch, a wine bottle, a helmet), and each carries a short vignette about a Fatui member in the Tsaritsa's Snezhnaya: Sandrone, Pulcinella, Capitano, Dottore and Pantalone.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: 2-piece gives +18% ATK; the 4-piece boosts CRIT Rate and Stellar Swirl reaction damage after triggering Stellar Swirl.

209.content:
Scion of the Blazing Sun: Scion of the Blazing Sun is a 4-star bow: an ancient longbow from King Deshret's era, carved with indecipherable ancient text and solemn patterns. Its story traces the priests of King Deshret's kingdom, their archery, and the descendants who still keep the old ceremonies in secret.

Lore: In the era when the desert king ruled the land, authority covered it like sunlight over the dunes. The nomads' surviving songs sing of that golden age, and say the red lord once contended against the bright sun and fell to the earth like a meteorite. Some priests were not slain by the kings and princes who followed and passed down King Deshret's art of archery.

Owners: No in-world owner is named. The wiki notes Sethos wields the ascended bow in his character introduction, which is promotional use only.

210.content: Scroll of Streaming Song (also: Streaming Song): Scroll of Streaming Song is a three-volume set of torn pages from desert ruins, kept in the House of Daena. It tells how the Mistress of Pushpavatika visits a wise princess and tests her with three riddles. Scholars have added notes on its translation and gaps.

key: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City
211.comment: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City
211.content:
Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City (also: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City artifact set, Beast Tamer's Talisman, Mountain Ranger's Marker, Mystic's Gold Dial, Wandering Scholar's Claw Cup, Demon-Warrior's Feather Mask): Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from Natlan, added in Version 5.0. Its five pieces belong to members of one band of adventurers: a beast tamer, a mountain ranger, a young mystic, a scholar and a warrior who set out in the Cataclysm for a legendary Abyss-repelling treasure in a ruined ancient city. It boosts Nightsoul Burst and elemental-reaction team play.

Lore: The pieces are the last belongings of people from different tribes who tried to reach a treasure in the ash-laden ancient city while the black tide ravaged Natlan, and most of them did not return.

212.content:
Serenitea Pot (also: Realm Within, The Realm Within, Teapot realm, Ode-of-Dust Teapot, Chen'ge Hu, Serenitea Pot realm): The Serenitea Pot is a small teapot the adeptus Madame Ping gives the Traveler in Liyue Harbor as thanks for helping save the city. Inside is a private pocket world made with the adeptal art of Sub-Space Creation, where the Traveler can build a house, garden and grounds and rest from the road. It is kept by a courteous finch-like teapot spirit named Tubby, who calls herself a butler.

Lore: Madame Ping used Sub-Space Creation, an adeptal ability she says was a blessing from Rex Lapis, to make a small autonomous world. The Traveler first walked through one such teapot in the Archon Quest, when she tested them while they collected the Cleansing Bell. After the Osial crisis she learned the Traveler camped outdoors and prepared a gift, with Yanfei running errands for the materials. Tubby, the teapot spirit, introduces the realm.

213.content:
Serpent Spine: Serpent Spine is a 4-star claymore from the Battle Pass Gnostic Hymn, in the game since Version 1.0. The in-game short description calls it a rare weapon from the ancient ocean whose swings carry the sound of ageless waves. The full text says it is a greatsword made from the spine of a great sea monster and tells of a singing sea captain who never returned from the deep.

Lore: In the stormy seas of the ancient past, those who set out often never returned. A greatsword-wielding captain, fond of drinking and merriment before voyages, sailed off on the day sea and wind aligned and neither he nor his ship came back.

214.content: Severed Fragment of Ikhor (also: Fragment of Ikhor, Ikhor's Fragment, Ikhor's power): The Severed Fragment of Ikhor is a quest item found in Snezhnaya (added in 7.0). Its description calls it a piece of Ikhor's power, split off by Aksinya when a "ritual" was interrupted, and notes it has taken the form of a glowing doll.

215.content:
Shimenawa's Reminiscence (also: Shimenawa's Reminiscence artifact set, Entangling Bloom, Shaft of Remembrance, Morning Dew's Moment, Hopeful Heart, Capricious Visage): Shimenawa's Reminiscence is a 4 and 5 star Inazuma artifact set. Its five item texts are the first-person memories of the shrine maiden Hibiki of her teacher the Kitsune Saiguu at the Grand Narukami Shrine, of fortune slips and paper-cord charms, and of the friends who were lost. It boosts ATK and trades Energy for Normal, Charged and Plunging Attack damage.

Lore: The narrator came to Narukami as a country shrine maiden and was trained by the Kitsune Saiguu, who spoke in riddles about entanglement, memory and loss. Years later Saiguu is gone, and the narrator holds the empty pipe and keeps a promise to someone who is not at her side.

216.content:
Silken Moon's Serenade (also: Crystal Tear of the Wanderer, Pristine Plume of the Blessed, Frost Devotee's Delirium, Joyous Glory of the Pure, Holy Crown of the Believer): Silken Moon's Serenade is a 4- and 5-star artifact set tied to Lunar reactions and the Moonsign. Its five pieces carry one narrator's account of the far north: the night Hyperborea's golden realm was destroyed by dark blue crystal nails, the pity of the Frost Moon's mistress, and the later suffering of the Frostmoon Scions, down to the Moonchanter Aila and her sister. It was released in version 6.0.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: 2-piece gives +20% Energy Recharge; the 4-piece gives party Elemental Mastery when a Moonsign is active and boosts Lunar Reaction DMG.

217.content: Silver Light (also: Radiance on the Water): Silver Light is a four-star sword obtained from the limited-time Version 7.1 event Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon (part of the Moonchase Festival). Its description says it is a longsword left by Wind Reader, one of the Three Hermits of Guizang. The item story shows him as a reckless young thaumaturge humbled and gently taken in by the swallow adeptus.

218.content:
Silvershower Heartstrings (also: Dryas's Nocturne): Silvershower Heartstrings is a 5-star bow, the legendary bow of the fairies, said to touch the hearts of listeners whether on stage or on the battlefield.

Lore: Fontainian playwrights liken strings to hearts, and the word heartstring appears in one of the oldest plays, Dryas, though the string there was a bowstring.

Owners: No owner is named. The bow is attributed to the fairies in legend.

219.content: Skyward Atlas (also: Cloud Atlas, Wandering Clouds): Skyward Atlas is a five-star catalyst of the Mondstadt Skyward series, released in 1.0. It is a cloud atlas that symbolises Dvalin and his former master, the Anemo Archon, details the winds and clouds of the northern regions and holds the power of sky and wind. In its story it is a copy of a far older atlas of 100,000 odes, each naming one cloud or wind.

220.content: Skyward Blade (also: Sky-Piercing Fang): Skyward Blade is a five-star sword of the Mondstadt Skyward series, released in 1.0. It is the sword of a knight and symbolises the restored honour of Dvalin, with the Anemo Archon's blessing on its fuller. Its story is Dvalin's fight with the shadow dragon Durin and the poison that followed.

221.content: Skyward Harp (also: Echoing Ballad, Sky-Piercing Lyre): Skyward Harp is a five-star bow of the Mondstadt Skyward series, released in 1.0. The item calls it the sky-piercing lyre: its story is how Barbatos' lyre drew Dvalin to him, held back the shadow dragon, and then went unheard by a poisoned Dvalin.

222.content: Skyward Pride (also: Sky-Ripping Dragon Spine): Skyward Pride is a five-star claymore of the Mondstadt Skyward series, released in 1.0. It symbolises the pride of Dvalin soaring through the skies and hums deeply when swung, with the force of his command of sky and wind. Its story tells of the battle with Durin, the poison, and Dvalin's fall to become Stormterror.

223.content:
Skyward Spine: Skyward Spine is a 5-star polearm, part of the Mondstadt series of weapons. Its item text is a short legend of the dragon Dvalin: he fought and killed the shadow dragon Durin in the skies over Mondstadt, but swallowed Durin's venom and spent the following centuries wounded in an ancient ruin. Added in Version 1.0.

Lore: In olden times the shadow dragon Durin envied Mondstadt's peace and came to defile it. His black wings darkened the sky and released toxic fumes that even the thousand winds could not hold back, so poisoned black rain fell on the people. The Anemo Archon heard their agony and called Dvalin to his side.

224.content:
Snow-Tombed Starsilver (also: Snow Tombed Starsilver): Snow-Tombed Starsilver is a 4-star claymore of the Dragonspine series, in-game description "an ancient greatsword stored between frescoes" and forged from Starsilver. Its text tells of the princess of the snow-entombed mountain city of Sal Vindagnyr, who gave it to a hero from another land. Added in Version 1.2.

Lore: When the verdant city was sealed by cloud and mist and unending snowstorms blotted out the moonlight, a nail that fell from the azure skies pierced all life and every interrupted story. The priest's daughter gave the Starsilver greatsword to the hero from another land, Imunlaukr.

225.content:
Solar Pearl: Solar Pearl is a 4-star catalyst of the Kunwu series, a dull golden pearl of unknown substance that harbours the light of the sun and moon and pulses with warm strength. It is rumoured to be a legendary orb of Liyue. It has been in the game since Version 1.0.

Lore: The text says it once absorbed all the light in the world and was then kept in a wooden box for millennia, yet its power has not dissipated. Released from its container, it shines on, and a truly knowledgeable sage might unleash its power after so long.

226.content:
Song of Broken Pines: Song of Broken Pines is a 5-star claymore, part of the Millennial Movement series. Its item text is a history of Mondstadt's rebel songs: how bards and a split Church of Favonius stood against the tyrant Decarabian and the ruling aristocracy, and how a folk song gained a second, defiant half when the rebellion rose. Added in Version 1.5.

Lore: The text opens with a folk song urging people to toss coins to the bard, give a bouquet to a fair maiden, drink bitter wine and sing for tomorrow. Mondstadt, the text says, is a land where songs travel on the wind, so tyrants such as Decarabian and the ruling aristocrats sometimes banned certain chords and tunes, sensing resistance in the bards' music.

227.content:
Song of Days Past (also: Forgotten Oath of Days Past, Recollection of Days Past, Echoing Sound From Days Past, Promised Dream of Days Past, Poetry of Days Past): Song of Days Past is a 4- and 5-star artifact set from Fontaine, added in Version 4.3. Its bonuses reward healing: it records healing as a Yearning effect and turns it into extra damage. Its pieces tell of the people the Remurians called the "people of bygone times": the rebellion of a songstress against the golden authority, her search for a wish-granting Pure Grail, and the verses that later turned her into legend.

Lore: Before the Many Waters converged, Remuria's golden order crushed the tribes of the north; a songstress united them against it, swore to Egeria and later sought the Pure Grail. Centuries later, only poems and plays remembered it.

key: Dawn and Dusk by the Lake
228.content:
Splendor of Tranquil Waters (also: Hauteclaire, Dawn and Dusk by the Lake): Splendor of Tranquil Waters is a 5-star sword: a scepter around which pure water swirls, once a symbol of the highest authority over the seas. Its story belongs to Erinnyes, a figure of the age of Remuria.

Lore: A scepter that once symbolised supreme authority over the seas. It belonged to Erinnyes, who in the time of the great symphony united the people of the high waters against the gods.

Owners: Erinnyes, per the description. No present-day wielder is named.

229.content: Staff of Homa (also: Homa Staff, Hùmó zhī Zhàng): The Staff of Homa is a five-star polearm of Liyue: a "devilishly red" ritual staff from the Archon War era, when fire rites were used to cleanse the miasmas of dead gods. Item text says a merciful doctor was given it by a whispering flame and used it to burn away impurity and release the dead from their ill karma. Today it is carried by Hu Tao, the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's director, who inherited it through the Hu family.

230.content:
Staff of the Scarlet Sands: The Staff of the Scarlet Sands is a 5-star polearm of the Deshret series. The in-game description calls it one of a paired set of obsidian scepters that grant the right to lead the people of the desert, though no retainer now lives who can verify the proper appearance of these regalia. Its story is a monologue by King Deshret about how the world should be ordered, ending in his longing for a perfect world.

Lore: The narrator, speaking as a creator, lists how the world was made: the sun and three moons (as a woman once described them to him), weight so that sand sank into earth, and seven sage monks to rule the paths of earth, water and stars. After the original world's barriers fell and dark poison seeped in, spikes pierced the earth to heal it.

Owners: No owner is named in the text. Cyno appears with the ascended staff in his official art and character demo, and Candace with the unascended one in her wish art and TCG card (wiki trivia).

231.content:
Starcaller's Watch (also: Offering Unto Wind and Sun, Mirror of Night): Starcaller's Watch is a 5-star catalyst: a statue carved in the shape of an eagle, a sacred relic of the Masters of the Night-Wind passed down from generation to generation.

Lore: In an ancient, exalted contract the messenger of night chose a child with a star-bright soul, set a crown of eagle feathers on her brow, and charged her to guide a formless ancient people into night's slumber.

Owners: The Masters of the Night-Wind keep it as a sacred relic. The wiki names its first wielder as the Holy Sovereign who was Maghan's master.

232.content: Starsilver (also: Starsilver ore, Starsilver Ore): Starsilver is a rare, precious ore found only on Dragonspine, the snowbound mountain of Mondstadt. Its item text says it is formed by the mountain's unique geography and its ley lines. It is silvery, is worked in forges, and is also prized by artists as a pigment source.

233.content:
String of Pearls (also: String of Pearls play, Lian Xin Zhu): String of Pearls is a five-act Liyue opera script by Yun Jin, split into five volumes. It follows Zixin, a young fisherwoman, and Fan Jie, a dock worker who returns her lost string of pearls. A misunderstanding, a false reward notice, a local bully named Wu Wang and a rescue in a dark stronghold bring them together.

Lore: Act I, Of Fish and Water: Zixin, sixteen by her own line, sells fish to support her ageing parents. She loses her string of pearls and Fan Jie, who found it, checks her wrist for wear marks. She takes this as an insult and scolds him before learning he meant well. He leaves before telling his full name, and she regrets it.

234.content:
Sturdy Bone (also: Trapper's Pride, Wanjiru's bone sword): Sturdy Bone is a 4-star longsword from Natlan, made of bone that has only grown harder with use. Legend says it was the hero Wanjiru's reliable weapon.

Lore: The great dragon that once ruled the land of flame had a tomb of bleached bone ridges like giant claws, patrolled by secret machines. Hearing of it around the tribe's fire, Wanjiru leaps for joy: nothing in the world was more fearsome, and surely she could find there the weapon she wanted most.

Owners: Wanjiru, by the text's legend. No later wielder is named.

235.content: Summit Shaper (also: Zhuófēng zhī Rèn, Blade of Mountain Cut): Summit Shaper is a five-star sword of Liyue and one of the Liyue series weapons tied to Rex Lapis in the Archon War. Item text says that in an age of turmoil, when people cried out for lost loved ones, the ruler of Geo carved a long blade from a slab of golden Cor Lapis, cut a corner off a mountain with one stroke, and on it swore a solemn oath: to gather the scattered and punish those who broke contracts.

236.content: Sunny Morning Sleep-In (also: Bathhouses, Hawks, and Narukami): Sunny Morning Sleep-In is a five-star catalyst, a bell lantern forged from purple jade. The game description says that placed beside a pillow it brings sweet dreams. Its item story is a sad, quiet one about a shrine maiden who had the three auspicious "first dreams" of the new year before the Cataclysm, and whose dreams of bathhouses, hawks and the Narukami banner came to mean loss.

237.content:
Surf's Up (also: Aqua Remembrance, Scorching Summer): Surf's Up is a 5-star catalyst: a commemorative prize reserved for the champion of the First All-Tribe Surfing Championship, kept at the Leisurely Puffer while the tournament is being prepared.

Lore: A huge black Volcano Lord fouled the springs of the People of the Springs by dumping his filth into them. The Pyro Archon Cochanina, a surfing champion, left her famous blade at home, took only a surfboard, and tricked him out to sea.

Owners: No wielder is named. Mualani is the custodian of the prize, not its holder.

238.content:
Sword of Descension: Sword of Descension is a 4-star sword in the game since Version 1.0 and given by mail to players who start on PS4 or PS5. Its description says it does not appear to belong to this world, and the item text calls it proof that the Traveler came to Teyvat by special means.

Lore: The item text says only one who has challenged the "world" may wield such a sword, and that the Traveler wields it while searching for the answers hidden in this world.

239.content:
Sword of Narzissenkreuz (also: Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz, Hero's Blade): The Sword of Narzissenkreuz is a 4-star sword received after the Rowboat's Wake quest in Fontaine. In the story it is the holy blade of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, its power faded when that story ended.

Lore: A ceremonial sword of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. It was used in a ritual to separate mind from body and, in the Ordo's story, held reason itself.

Owners: Ann carries the blade in the story; the player receives the weapon at the end of the quest.

240.content:
Symphonist of Scents (also: Seasoned Symphony): Symphonist of Scents is a 5-star polearm: an elegantly built baton said to have been wielded by a great musician, Euergetia, to bridge tune and taste.

Lore: During the long conquest of the tribes and kingdoms of the High Sea by the Legion Athanatoi, the Harmost Euergetia listened to the pleas of the conquered. The homesick people, though awed by the golden capital, missed the cuisines they had once enjoyed.

Owners: Euergetia, per the description (she is called the benefactrix on Remurian engravings).

241.content: Tale of "Durin" (also: Tale of Durin, Durin's storybook, the book of Durin, Andersdotter's magic book): Tale of "Durin" is a quest item from the Draco Rubedo Chapter (6.2), Durin's Story Quest. It is a replica, made by the Hexenzirkel witch Alice, of the unfinished storybook left by Andersdotter ("M"), Durin's creator and mother. The original had to end up with Durin so he could write his own ending. The replica has no magical properties but keeps every twist of the story.

242.content:
Tales Carried by the Northwind (also: Tales Carried by the Northwind (book)): Tales Carried by the Northwind is a single-volume book left on a box near Kofitse in Piramida. Its in-game description calls it a poetry collection chronicling the deeds of successive Starshynas, mostly lost in past calamities, with only a small fraction of the original fragments recovered. The surviving poems are attributed to Silvestr Petrovich Solovei and Sergei Semyonovich Mayakov.

Lore: Silvestr Petrovich Solovei: two excerpted poems. In the first, a dying speaker thanks a listener, admits he trusted the nobles' deceptive words, and mourns comrades, homeland and loved ones resting in the night, then resolves to burn briefly as a beacon on the snowy borderlands. In the second, a Nightingale forges the first light on a summit against a dark tide of monsters, and the poem closes on generations, thunder, pine, tide and wind, who inherit the Starshyna name.

243.content: Tamayuratei no Ohanashi (also: Tamayuratei, the lantern youkai's polearm): Tamayuratei no Ohanashi is a four-star polearm of the Youkai series, obtained during the Version 5.4 event Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival. Its text tells of an invisible youkai who took the form of a spectral flame, stole stories at hearths and braziers and retold them at banquets of wandering spirits, and was named "Tamayuratei" by the kitsune chief Hakushin. After the Cataclysm it became a messenger of battle reports and wore itself away.

244.content:
Tenacity of the Millelith (also: Flower of Accolades, Ceremonial War-Plume, Orichalceous Time-Dial, Noble's Pledging Vessel, General's Ancient Helm): Tenacity of the Millelith is a 4- and 5-star artifact set for Liyue's soldiers. Its five pieces are a golden flower, a falcon-feather plume, a sun-and-moon time-dial, a golden oath cup and a general's helmet, and their item text commemorates the Millelith who held the Chasm against the Abyss alongside a nameless yaksha, dying there so civilians could escape.

Lore: The pieces recount how Millelith soldiers and a nameless yaksha made a last stand against the Abyss in the Chasm, and how Liyue still honours them.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: the 2-piece bonus raises HP; the 4-piece bonus gives the party an ATK and Shield Strength buff after an Elemental Skill hit.

245.content:
Teyvat Travel Guide (also: Teyvat Geographic Special Edition, Alice's Mondstadt Diaries, Alice's Travels in Liyue, Alice's Inazuma Diaries): The Teyvat Travel Guide is a three-volume magazine series from the Adventurers' Guild. Under the heading 'Teyvat Geographic Special Edition', each issue is a short travel diary by Alice, covering Mondstadt, Liyue and Inazuma. Alice is a cheerful experimenter and the diaries treat sightseeing as an excuse for explosives, potions and mischief.

Lore: Vol. 1 (Mondstadt) visits Dadaupa Gorge, Starsnatch Cliff, Windrise, Falcon Coast, the Whispering Woods, Brightcrown Canyon and Stormterror's Lair. Vol. 2 (Liyue) visits Dihua Marsh and Wangshu Inn, Guili Plains, Jueyun Karst, Yaoguang Shoal and Guyun Stone Forest. Vol. 3 (Inazuma) visits Mt. Yougou and the Grand Narukami Shrine, Inazuma City, Tatarasuna and Yashiori Island.

246.content: The Alley Flash (also: Alley Flash): The Alley Flash is a four-star sword of the Alley series: a straight, night-black longsword once carried by a thief who roamed Mondstadt's benighted streets. The item text tells of a young noble who stole it from his family's vault and used it, never staining it with blood, to rob the rich for the poor.

247.content: The Bell (also: Bell greatsword, clock greatsword): The Bell is a four-star claymore of the Wanderer's Troupe series. It is a heavy greatsword with a clock set into it, whose internal mechanisms are long damaged. Its story belongs to Kreuzlied, a former Lawrence clan noble turned traitor who travelled with the Troupe.

248.content:
The Black Sword (also: Black Sword): The Black Sword is a 4-star sword from the Battle Pass Gnostic Hymn, in the game since Version 1.0. The in-game short description calls it a pitch-black longsword that thirsts for violence and conflict. The full text is the parable of a bright white knight whose pursuit of justice slid into slaughter.

Lore: A blade that thirsts after fresh blood is awakened by its scent, and those who wield and nourish it keep killing until even a pure soul is blackened. The text tells of a white knight who rode to cut down injustice, beasts and fires, taught by the Wolf Pup in chivalry, justice and swordsmanship.

249.content:
The Byakuyakoku Collection (also: Byakuyakoku Collection, Collection of Byakuyakoku): The Byakuyakoku Collection is a five-volume set of old texts from Enkanomiya's Byakuyakoku era, obtained by completing the quest Collection of Dragons and Snakes. It holds a folk tale of the Profane Serpent, a creation chronicle, a hydrology study, vishap experiment records and a children's puzzle book.

Lore: - Vol. 1, "The Serpent and Drakes of Tokoyokoku": a novel based on Watatsumi folktales. The sage Aberaku brings a sun to Enkanomiya and is imprisoned by the first Sunchild; years later a child finds a vast serpent who becomes the people's god.
