- Vol. 2, "Before Sun and Moon": a restricted chronicle of the world's making and the people's fall into the dark.
- Vol. 3: a geography and hydrology of Byakuyakoku.
- Vol. 4: Bathysmal Vishap experiment records.
- Vol. 5: a children's riddle book.

250.content: "The Catch" (also: The Catch, Ako Domeki's harpoon, Zaemon's barbed spear): "The Catch" is a four-star polearm: the favoured barbed spear of a famous Inazuman bandit, Ako Domeki. It began as a harpoon for catching fish and proved handy in battle; item text says he even pierced the enchanted, sword-armed puppet with it before carrying it off. It is bought with fish from the Inazuma Fishing Association.

251.content: The Daybreak Chronicles (also: Daybreak Chronicles, Dawning Song of Daybreak): The Daybreak Chronicles is a five-star bow released in version 6.2 (2025-12-03), part of the Hexerei series. Its description calls it a bow whose strings gather the "songs of resistance" carried on the wind, strong enough to tear boundless darkness apart with the light of daybreak. Its item story is the legend of Kreuzlied, a name that Mondstadt turned from a byword for failed rebels into a rallying cry.

252.content:
The Exile (also: Exile's Flower, Exile's Feather, Exile's Pocket Watch, Exile's Goblet, Exile's Circlet): The Exile is an Energy Recharge artifact set (3 and 4 star, added 1.0), called Legacy in the Adventurer Handbook. Its five pieces mourn an aristocrat's carefree childhood, a family feud that wrecked his house, and a lonely exile in which he kept only a few treasured objects. The wiki links him to Parsifal and the Eberhart feud; the texts name no one.

Lore: An aristocrat lost his childhood to a family feud, left his house in disgrace and wandered alone, carrying little more than a few mementos.

key: The Fall of the Faded Castle
253.comment: The Fall of the Faded Castle
253.content:
The Fall of the Faded Castle (also: Fall of the Faded Castle (poem)): The Fall of the Faded Castle is a three-volume poem of Fontaine by an unknown author. It describes a nightmare black ship, a gilded castle by a lake where a fearful master held endless revels, and the night a dark-robed spirit destroyed it. It reads as a ghost story about a debt coming due.

Lore: Vol. 1: in a dream the narrator sees a black ship sailing through night and fog, its hull rotten and mast shattered but its pieces bound together with algae and seaweed into a shape no one can look at without panic. A tall, slim figure in dark robes stands on deck with cold, piercing eyes. The narrator asks whether it is a sea monster, a lord returned from an ancient world, or the nightmare itself.

254.content:
The First Great Magic: The First Great Magic is a 5-star bow: a stage prop once used by a past Great Magician, whose final secret was that it was also a weapon beyond the pale.

Lore: Parsifal the Great is the stage name of a Fontainian woman from the Fleuve Cendre, who performed with her sister Josephine as assistant. The name came from a thief in Master Coppelius's play, which the text calls an elusive thief who appears and disappears at will.

Owners: A past Great Magician, Parsifal, per the description.

255.content: The Flute (also: Flute sword): The Flute is a four-star sword of the Wanderer's Troupe series. It has a nimble, delicately engraved and perforated blade that sounded like a flute when swung with skill, the pitch depending on the swing angle. It is tied to a swordswoman of the Troupe later called the Dawnlight Swordswoman.

256.content:
The Folio of Foliage (also: Folio of Foliage): The Folio of Foliage is a three-volume devotional biography of the Dendro Archon during the Cataclysm, kept in the House of Daena in Sumeru. Its text and subject were rewritten after the Archon Quest Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies (3.2).

Lore: She weeps as a black tide of decay swallows the world, walks through a ruined forest that blooms under her feet, and goes into the broken heart of the desert to heal it.

key: The Fox in the Dandelion Sea
257.comment: The Fox in the Dandelion Sea
257.content:
The Fox in the Dandelion Sea (also: Fox in the Dandelion Sea, Foxtale): The Fox in the Dandelion Sea is an 11-part Mondstadt fairy tale told by a hunter. He spares a fox trapped by a Mist Flower, is led to a boundless sea of dandelions, and teaches the fox's child to speak the human tongue in return for the promise of transformation magic. The promise ends with him turned into a dandelion and blown home, and he wakes at the same lake.

Lore: A hunter near a village finds a white fox with its tail frozen in the ice by a Mist Flower and plans to turn it into stew, but its lake-like eyes make his arrow miss and the fox flees. That night the fox returns, becomes a tall black-haired woman and offers thanks. Days later she leads him through a storm of dandelion seeds to a sea of dandelions and asks him to teach her child human language in return for fox magic.

258.content:
The Legend of Vennessa (also: Legend of Vennessa): The Legend of Vennessa is a two-volume ballad collection popular since Mondstadt's reconstruction. It tells how Vennessa, a fire-haired woman enslaved under the aristocrats, prayed for freedom, was answered by the Anemo Archon Barbatos, and went on to defeat the drake and break the rulers' tower. She is remembered as the founder of the Knights of Favonius.

Lore: Vol. 1 sets the scene of old Mondstadt as a dungeon under royal chains, where festivities were the rich's vanity games. It introduces Vennessa as a fiery-headed woman from the southern plains, born free but imprisoned, who still prayed for her people and Mondstadt. Vol. 2 tells that Barbatos descended to her, said every being deserves a name and offered friendship; she marched to battle to his singing, the demonic dragon fled, and the aristocrats cowered.

key: The Legends of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire
259.comment: The Legends of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire
259.content:
The Legends of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire (also: Legends of Reed Miller, Reed Miller pulp stories): The Legends of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire is a three-volume anthology of pulp stories about the master thief Reed Miller, sold by Dhabit at Mimisbrunnr Books in Nasha Town and described as wildly popular across Nod-Krai. The description warns that the stories are collated from various works and authors, and that their truth is as dubious as the paper.

Lore: Vol. 1: An issue of a ten-Mora magazine serial in which Miller plans to steal the Frostmoon relic, the Sampo Mill, from the governor's palace in Piramida. Chapter IV has the rival thief Wagtail confront him; in Chapter XVII a disguised Miller has the governor arrested and returns the treasure to the Frostmoon Scions.

key: The Little Witch and the Undying Fire
Little Witch and the Undying Fire
260.comment: The Little Witch and the Undying Fire
260.content:
The Little Witch and the Undying Fire (also: Little Witch and the Undying Fire): The Little Witch and the Undying Fire is a seven-volume storybook written in turns by members of the Hexenzirkel, the circle of long-lived witches. It follows a young witch who draws the exam topic 'find the undying fire', travels through odd adventures, and finally finds it in an old, dying witch who is the last star still burning. It is a jokey fable that turns into an elegy.

Lore: Vol. 1: a young witch draws the exam topic 'find the undying fire'. Vol. 2: under a blood-green moon she meets a fortune teller and watches the witches' forbidden Night Carnival. Vols. 3 and 4: she hunts and captures demon kings. Vol. 5 (one line): her teacher says the trial is over. Vol. 6: Octavia says the cosmos is dying and the fire exists. Vol. 7: at the end of the universe the old witch is the last star burning, and the little witch carries her flame home.

261.content:
The Mondstadt Tower (also: Mond Tower novel): The Mondstadt Tower is a one-volume historical romance novel set in the dark age of Mondstadt's aristocrats. Its blurb promises a fateful meeting between an outlander girl and an ominous orphan. The text that survives in-game follows the singer Ines, who throws the Harpastum at Ludi Harpastum, and the Seneschal and his adopted son Octave.

Lore: In the time of the aristocrats a high tower stood in Mondstadt's plaza. It was nominally built to honour Barbatos but was really a show of wealth. The one comfort of the commoners was Ludi Harpastum. At one festival a wandering singer from a distant land, Ines, was admired for her beauty and her songs, and she gave her festival earnings to the poor and orphans. The frail Seneschal fell for her at first sight, but his piety and the Church's claim to aid the poor made him angry, and he plotted to confine her in the Cathedral.

key: The Pale Princess and the Six Pygmies
Pale Princess and the Six Pygmies
262.comment: The Pale Princess and the Six Pygmies
262.content:
The Pale Princess and the Six Pygmies (also: Pale Princess and the Six Pygmies, Pale Princess and Six Pygmies): A seven-volume fairy tale said to have been told across Teyvat for ages. Only Vol. 1 can be read in game. Lisa gives the Mondstadt library's copy to the Traveler as 'custodian' after retrieving it from the Abyss Order.

Lore: Vol. 1: long ago the Night Mother ruled the Land of Night, where no light, trees or life but dark horrors existed. Only the Moonlight Forest escaped her rule, its people fair, light-haired and blue-eyed.

263.content: The Saga of Hamavaran (also: Saga of Hamavaran, Hamavaran Saga): The Saga of Hamavaran is a three-volume light novel by the writer Pursina, sold at the Yae Publishing House in Inazuma City. It follows a Sumeru scholar named Hamavaran who travels to Inazuma.

264.content: The Stringless (also: Stringless harp bow): The Stringless is a four-star bow of the Wanderer's Troupe series: an exquisite stringed instrument that is also a bow, once played by the Troupe's harpist from Fontaine. After the Troupe disbanded its harp strings were cut, leaving only the bowstring.

265.content:
The Tale of Kuntur (also: Tale of Kuntur): A one-volume Natlan folk tale, sequel to The Tale of Qoyllor and Ukuku. Kuntur, their shunned son with no Saurian companion, defeats the sorcerer Rumi and wins an Iktomisaurus partner.

Lore: Blind Ukuku raised young Kuntur alone; the tribe shunned them because clouds followed them. Kuntur found no Iktomisaurus willing to join him. When the sorcerer Rumi stole the tribe's Saurians, Kuntur volunteered, defeated him and won a companion.

key: The Tale of Qoyllor and Ukuku
266.comment: The Tale of Qoyllor and Ukuku
266.content:
The Tale of Qoyllor and Ukuku (also: Tale of Qoyllor and Ukuku): A one-volume Natlan folk tale, once told orally, obtained in the quest To Wish Upon a Star. Star-child Qoyllor falls to earth and Ukuku, a silent hunter, helps her search for her lost power.

Lore: Curious Qoyllor fell from her star and her power, given by her father the Sun, shattered across the land. The hunter Ukuku promised to help find the shards. When she learned he had hidden some to keep her, she left; the Sun took her back and blinded him.

key: The Tale of Shiruyeh and Shirin
267.comment: The Tale of Shiruyeh and Shirin
267.content: The Tale of Shiruyeh and Shirin (also: Tale of Shiruyeh and Shirin, Shiruyeh and Shirin): The Tale of Shiruyeh and Shirin is a two-volume story told by a Jinni in a magic bottle to the shepherd she calls Raven, found in the House of Daena. It tells how the hero Kisra Parvezravan became king of Gurabad, how his father-in-law's line died in one night, and how his son Shiruyeh killed him.

268.content: The Unforged (also: Sword of No Work, Sword of No Skill): The Unforged is a five-star claymore of the Liyue series, an edgeless blade whose description says it can drive away evil spirits and wicked people. Its item story is a legend of an ancient stone dragon in Liyue, and says the sword was planted as a seal beside the tree that subdued it.

269.content:
The Viridescent Hunt: The Viridescent Hunt is a 4-star bow from the Battle Pass Gnostic Hymn, in the game since Version 1.0. The in-game short description calls it a pure green hunting bow that once belonged to a hunter whose home was the forest. The full text is the tale of a nameless hunter taught never to loose an arrow for anything but survival.

Lore: The hunter was raised, far from the city, to live by the laws of nature, never bearing ill will and loosing arrows only to survive. She left no traces and comforted wounded beasts until their lives returned to nature.

key: The Volcano Lord and the Shadow Pins
Volcano Lord and the Shadow Pins
270.comment: The Volcano Lord and the Shadow Pins
270.content:
The Volcano Lord and the Shadow Pins (also: Volcano Lord and the Shadow Pins): A woven scroll in Natlan about the hero Traore. Elder Traore traps the Volcano Lord's arm and pins it with four giant nails, creating the Shadow Pins of the Sulfurous Veins.

Lore: The Volcano Lord, a black-and-purple salamander-shaped giant, took over the Great Volcano of Tollan and tormented the tribes. Learning it meant to swallow the Children of Echoes' gems, Elder Traore baited it into a trap at the Sulfurous Veins and it lost an arm.

271.content: The Widsith (also: Widsith notebook): The Widsith is a four-star catalyst of the Wanderer's Troupe series: a heavy notebook of hand-written musical scores and travel journals, moth-eaten and worn, that the Troupe shared. It records their experiences and still carries power drawn from their performances.

272.content:
Thundering Fury (also: Thundering Fury artifact set, Thunderbird's Mercy, Survivor of Catastrophe, Hourglass of Thunder, Omen of Thunderstorm, Thunder Summoner's Crown): Thundering Fury is an Electro artifact set (4 and 5 star). Its five pieces tell, in fragments, of an ancient tribe that worshipped the Thunderbird, a violet-lightning bird. A young lad who sang to the bird became a blood sacrifice, and the enraged Thunderbird destroyed the tribe. The set is earned in the Midsummer Courtyard domain.

Lore: The tribe feared the Thunderbird and thanked it for its blessings, and shamans offered blood to it for protection and forgiveness. The texts insist the bird was a monster that did not care for human worship, and the tribe took its unpredictable moves for divine revelations.

273.content: Thundering Pulse (also: Rule By Thunder, the Shogun's bow): Thundering Pulse is a five-star bow, a longbow with eternal lightning crackling around it that the game calls a gift from the Shogun. Its item story follows the samurai Takamine the Mistsplitter, who won it from a Great Tengu in a gamble, learned Tengu archery from it, and left it as a wager with a shrine maiden when he went to face the disaster from across the sea. He did not return as himself.

274.content:
Thundersoother (also: Thundersoother's Heart, Thundersoother's Plume, Hour of Soothing Thunder, Thundersoother's Goblet, Thundersoother's Diadem, Flower of Thunder): Thundersoother is an Electro artifact set from launch (Midsummer Courtyard domain). Its five pieces recount a legendary hero, "the Thundersoother", who conquered thunder and lightning, killed the tyrannical Beast of Thunder, and later lived and died alone.

Lore: The Beast of Thunder once enslaved people with its lightning. The Thundersoother, who plucked the purple Flower of Thunder with reverence and wore it on his chest, fought the beast without wavering and defeated it in a lightning storm, beheading it and claiming a diadem as his trophy.

275.content: Tidal Shadow: Tidal Shadow is a four-star claymore of the Beaumont series, forged in Fontaine. The description calls it an exquisitely crafted standard-model sword for the high-ranking officers and flagship captains of Fontaine's old navy. Its story recalls the white ironclad flagship Sponsian and Admiral Basil Elton, whose blue-and-white blade is all that remained of the fleet's legend.

276.content:
Tome of the Eternal Flow (also: Aeon Wave): Tome of the Eternal Flow is a 5-star catalyst: a manual once passed down from generation to generation within an underwater priory. Today none know of its existence.

Lore: The first watcher led new recruits to recite an oath: remember the oath of a thousand years, defend the foundation of the capital of water, and never forget the sin that was once tempting as honey nor the responsibility that may feel like fetters.

Owners: No owner is named; it was passed on within the priory.

277.content: Toukabou Shigure (also: Toukabou, the cursed parasol): Toukabou Shigure is a four-star sword of the Youkai series, designed as an umbrella and obtained during the Version 3.3 event Akitsu Kimodameshi. Its text is a ghost story ("kaidan") told by a woman from Fontaine: a dancer's cherished umbrella becomes cursed after two deaths, turns into a one-eyed, one-legged, long-tongued youkai, and is finally washed and enshrined by a young shrine maiden.

key: Treasured Tales of the Chouken Shinkageuchi
278.comment: Treasured Tales of the Chouken Shinkageuchi
278.content:
Treasured Tales of the Chouken Shinkageuchi (also: Shinkageuchi, Chouken Shinkageuchi): Treasured Tales of the Chouken Shinkageuchi is a one-volume traditional Inazuman novel sold at the Yae Publishing House in Inazuma City. Also called "Shinkageuchi", it was once restricted. It tells a fantastical story of the first Shogun and her kagemusha, praising the first Shogun's wisdom and the kagemusha's valor.

Lore: The book opens with the Goshintou ceremony. When Narukami came to her people she brought the craft of swordmaking; after thousands of years mortal smiths could make swords that pleased her. The Grand Narukami Shrine and the Shogunate therefore gather the finest swords and offer them to the shrine, naming them "Goshintou".

279.content:
Tulaytullah's Remembrance: Tulaytullah's Remembrance is a 5-star catalyst: a bell of deep sapphire and sterling silver whose echoes are "as crisp as they are distant". Its story recalls the Sapphire City Tulaytullah, home of the Tighnarians, and the farewell of the court dancer Makhaira to her golden-eyed lover Xiphos, and what became of both of them.

Lore: Once, on the silver dunes, a woman danced with the three sisters of the moon; blood and tears mingled to form a garden spring. The Lord of Flowers grieved, and a sapphire city rose from her tears, where the Tighnarians grew proud and bred generations of wisdom. Tulaytullah was said to be her most precious jewel, and in the golden age even the moon looked amber.

Owners: No owner is named; the bell is a memory-object of Tulaytullah. Xiphos and Makhaira are the people the story is about.

key: Mourning Bell of the Undying One
280.content:
Undying One's Mourning Bell (also: Sigurd's bell, Mourning Bell of the Undying One): The Undying One's Mourning Bell is a bronze bell carried by Sigurd, a Lightkeeper warrior who fought the Wild Hunt in Nod-Krai and, in the item's words, walked through the dark abyss. Its peal is said to be heard on pitch-black nights. The Traveler recovers it as a quest item and returns it to his grave, and it also exists as the Sands piece of the Long Night's Oath artifact set.

Lore: Sigurd was a formidable Lightkeeper who fought the Wild Hunt to the end. The bell is the sound of his stubborn watch: folk tales hold that whenever mournful bells toll, the one who swore to hunt the Wild Hunt is near.

key: The Wine-Flask Over Which the Plan Was Hatched
281.content:
Unfinished Reverie (also: Unfinished Reverie artifact set, Dark Fruit of Bright Flowers, Faded Emerald Tail, Moment of Attainment, The Wine-Flask Over Which the Plan Was Hatched, Crownless Crown): Unfinished Reverie is a 4- and 5-star artifact set, added in Version 4.6, whose lore belongs to Natlan. Its pieces tell of the scarlet-eyed youth who gathered heroes against an insane king, and of a young girl, twin heroes, a taciturn warrior and a scarred craftsman who helped him. The final piece shows the girl grown old and erasing the craftsman's name. Its bonuses reward fighting Burning enemies with off-field damage.

Lore: The pieces recount an uprising against a mad king of a city of ash, carried out by a few heroes and an artisan who left no name.

282.content: Uraku Misugiri (also: Misugiri, Brocade Bloom, Shrine Sword): Uraku Misugiri is a five-star sword made by the renowned literato Urakusai, a Kitsune. Legend says that in hundreds of years it has never cut any living creature. The name comes from an episode where a drunken Urakusai sliced the gold-lacquered stage curtains of the bake-danuki in a dance, and the sword was later given as a reward to the man known as the Otogi King, "he of the Front Gate".

key: Many Oaths of Dawn and Dusk
283.content:
Verdict (also: Many Oaths of Dawn and Dusk): Verdict is a 5-star claymore of Fontaine, released in Version 4.3 alongside Navia. Its item text tells of Leticia, the eldest daughter of the noble House Randolph, who slipped into the underground Fleuve Cendre in disguise, fell in love with a young man there, and eventually abandoned her family name to live among its people. The weapon is described as stained with the blood of enemies and loved ones alike.

Lore: A young noblewoman, Leticia, is told by her father that as the eldest daughter of House Randolph she must keep a composed, pure bearing, because when nobles fall they drag many common homes down with them. She still disguises herself and goes down to the Fleuve Cendre, the sunless subterranean city. A man there sees through the disguise and invites her to see how its people live.

Owners: The text names Leticia as the weapon's former user ("a young maiden who forsook her family name"). No present-day character is established as owning the original.

284.content:
Vermillion Hereafter (also: Flowering Life, Feather of Nascent Light, Solar Relic, Moment of the Pact, Thundering Poise): Vermillion Hereafter is a 4- and 5-star artifact set that boosts ATK after an Elemental Burst. Its five pieces (Flowering Life, Feather of Nascent Light, Solar Relic, Moment of the Pact, Thundering Poise) have item text about the Chasm in Liyue: the mountain tribes' plea to a four-armed yaksha, the Millelith soldiers who marched into the abyss, and the battle that ended with the yaksha and many soldiers lost.

Lore: The pieces follow a legend of the Chasm: a four-armed yaksha answers the tribes' plea and fights the darkness there, supported by Millelith soldiers who do not return.

Gameplay: Game mechanics: the 2-piece bonus raises ATK; the 4-piece bonus gives an ATK buff after an Elemental Burst that grows as the wearer loses HP.

285.content:
Viridescent Venerer (also: In Remembrance of Viridescent Fields, Viridescent Arrow Feather, Viridescent Venerer's Determination, Viridescent Venerer's Vessel, Viridescent Venerer's Diadem): Viridescent Venerer is an Anemo artifact set from launch (Valley of Remembrance domain). Its five pieces tell of a legendary huntress, the "queen of hunters", who moved silently through the forest, stopped hunting animals at a boy's request after disaster struck an ancient kingdom, and hunted monsters instead.

Lore: In the days when monsters had not yet appeared, the Viridescent Venerer hid her human scent with a white wild flower, and was sought by walking barefoot through the forest. The one who found her was a boy, when disaster had just befallen an ancient kingdom. She had once let the grass and mud tell her what birds and roots perceived, but when the God of the Woods died in the disaster the plants stopped speaking, so she used a wayfinding device. At the boy's request she stopped hunting birds and beasts and hunted the monsters that brought suffering instead.

286.content:
Vivid Notions (also: Falling Rainbow's Wish, Dawn's First Hue, Twilight's Splendor): Vivid Notions is a 5-star catalyst: a trophy of gemstones from the Collective of Plenty and crystals from the Flower-Feather Clan, said to have belonged to a legendary wrestler.

Lore: After the six heroes of the blazing sun had stepped into the night wind, the tribes quarrelled over the empty throne. A girl who had stood silently in Wanjiru's shadow burst into the council chamber and drove a half-broken bone blade into the long table, ending the quarrel.

Owners: The description says the trophy once belonged to a legendary wrestler; the story is about Fietena.

287.content: Vortex Vanquisher (also: Guànhóng zhī Shuò, Rainbow-Piercing Lance): Vortex Vanquisher is a five-star polearm of Liyue and the weapon Zhongli is shown with. Its item story is a sailors' legend from the days when ships sailed beside sea monsters: Rex Lapis once wielded a spear that pierced the rainbow and pinned a churning vortex in the middle of the deep sea, and whales and dolphins still gather there to sing.

288.content:
Vourukasha's Glow (also: Stamen of Khvarena's Origin, Vibrant Pinion, Ancient Abscission, Feast of Boundless Joy, Heart of Khvarena's Brilliance): Vourukasha's Glow is a Sumeru artifact set (Version 3.6, Molten Iron Fortress domain). Its five pieces trace the Khvarena, a daughter-like shard of life made by the Goddess of Flowers: she is entrusted to the queen of grass and trees, forged into the divine bird Simurgh, and finally shatters into the countless flowers of the Vourukasha Oasis. The set is a farewell, not a chronicle.

Lore: A mother warns her "innocent daughter", the Khvarena, of a faceless nightmare in her dreams and sends her to "another mother", a verdant queen of grass and trees whose light is brighter than her own. The Khvarena will face division and death before becoming immortal, and the lord of sweet dew and the lord of grass and trees will lose their divine forms and be forgotten.

289.content:
Wanderer's Troupe (also: Troupe's Dawnlight, Bard's Arrow Feather, Concert's Final Hour, Wanderer's String-Kettle, Conductor's Top Hat, Wanderer's Troupe artifact set): Wanderer's Troupe is a 4- and 5-star artifact set (1.0) about a troupe of travelling warrior-musicians from about a thousand years ago, who used swords for flutes and bows for harps and played for both friends and foes. They recorded their travels in a book called The Widsith. The wiki connects them to a failed uprising against Mondstadt's aristocracy.

Lore: A troupe of swordswoman, harpist-archer and conductor wandered the world, playing music with weapons. Its members died one by one and their instruments were buried in dust.

290.content:
Wandering Evenstar: Wandering Evenstar is a 4-star catalyst: originally a device used by researchers to observe and calculate celestial phenomena, which now serves as a conduit and catalyst. Its legend is of a prince who lost his kingdom and wandered into the rainforest.

Lore: The tale is set thousands of years ago, after the foolish God-King was buried by sandstorms. The wandering prince, having lost his kingdom, retreated into the rainforest, meaning to conquer new lands but pursued by a huntress with a white bow. Trapped by vine branches in cold moonlight, he heard a tiger growl around him.

Owners: No owner is named, and no character is recorded wielding it.

291.content: Wavebreaker's Fin (also: Umigozen's naginata, Ayame's naginata): Wavebreaker's Fin is a four-star polearm of the Watatsumi series. Item text calls it the naginata of "Umigozen", a mighty Watatsumi warrior, whose edge flows with the phosphorescence of the deep. Narukami's navies are recorded in the island's music as having quailed before her. It is the only proof that she once tried to change the tides of the world.

292.content:
Waveriding Whirl (also: Fangs Flying To and Fro, Tupac's boomerang): Waveriding Whirl is a 4-star catalyst from Natlan: a boomerang made from a giant sea serpent's fangs. It was a rare weapon that the giant Tupac called "trusty".

Lore: Tupac of the Meztli towered like a mountain, with a sandstone-like body and a burning heart whose steam nearly hid the sun. In an age of peace, when even the ancient shadow-foe was silent, he was sullen, longing to have been born in the age of Xbalanque's dragon-slaying or among those who fought the Python King.

Owners: Tupac, the giant of the Meztli, by the text.

293.content:
Bow (also: Bows, bow users): The Bow is one of the five weapon types in Genshin Impact, and each playable character is bound to exactly one type. Bow users fight at long range with quick arrow volleys and aimed shots. A fully charged aimed shot carries the wielder's element, so a bow wielder with a Vision fights as an elemental sniper.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): Bow users make long-range attacks. The Normal Attack chain is 3 to 6 quick shots whose paths are fixed once fired, so they can miss a moving target.

294.content:
Catalyst (also: Catalysts, catalyst users): The Catalyst is one of the five weapon types in Genshin Impact, and each playable character is bound to exactly one type. Catalyst users cast magic from range through a focus such as a book or an orb. Both their Normal and Charged Attacks deal elemental damage, so their attacks carry the wielder's own element.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): all Normal and Charged Attacks of a Catalyst user deal elemental damage, and the element matches the wielder's own Vision or natural element. A Normal Attack chain is usually 3 to 4 ranged elemental attacks.

295.content:
Claymore (also: Claymores, greatsword): The Claymore is one of the five weapon types in Genshin Impact, and each playable character is bound to exactly one type. Claymores are big two-handed weapons: slower than swords and polearms but heavier per hit, with strong interruption and the ability to break shields and Geo objects.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): Claymores restrict the wielder to slower hits than other melee weapons but deal more damage per hit with higher interruption. A Normal Attack chain is typically 3 to 5 slow, wide, powerful attacks.

296.content:
Polearm (also: Polearms): The Polearm is one of the five weapon types in Genshin Impact, and each playable character is bound to exactly one type. Polearms are long-reaching melee weapons with fast attacks and moderate damage per hit.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): polearms have fast attacks, long forward reach and moderate damage per hit. A Normal Attack chain is typically 3 to 6 fast melee attacks.

297.content:
Sword (also: Swords): The Sword is one of the five weapon types in Genshin Impact, and each playable character is bound to exactly one type. Swords are the middle ground of melee weapons, with attack speed and damage comparable to polearms but a shorter reach.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): a Sword Normal Attack chain is typically 3 to 5 fast melee attacks with relatively short reach.

298.content: Whitelake Frostfeather (also: Snow Swan's Finale): Whitelake Frostfeather is a five-star sword added in version 7.0. The in-game description calls it a longsword as light as a snow swan's feathers that stays pure and untainted. Its story is an academic note about two older scripts, a "white" and a "black" one, on which the ballet Black Snow Swan draws, in which a tempter hands a young woman a sword.

299.content:
Wind Glider (also: Wind Gliders, Wings of First Flight, gliding license, gliding licence): The Wind Glider is a pair of wing-like frames that lets a person glide on the air. In Mondstadt, the city of wind, gliding is a beloved skill: the Knights of Favonius' Outriders use gliders constantly, and Amber gives the Traveler their first pair, the Wings of First Flight, when they arrive in the city.

Lore: Gliders come from Mondstadt. The Wings of First Flight were a pair Amber had long saved for a promising junior knight; she gave them to the Traveler, an outlander she chose to believe in.

300.content: Windblume Ode (also: Windblume bow): Windblume Ode is a four-star bow obtained during the limited-time Invitation of Windblume event (Version 1.4). It is adorned with nameless flowers and carries the hopes of an equally nameless person. Its item text recounts the Windblume as a flower of resistance in the days of the tyrant in the tower.

301.content:
Windsong Lyre (also: Mondstadt lyre): The Windsong Lyre is a plucked, lyre-style instrument from Mondstadt that the Traveler can play as a gadget. Its in-game text calls it a traditional Mondstadt instrument of fine workmanship, made for able hands. It first appeared in Version 1.4 during the Invitation of Windblume event.

Lore: The item text says Mondstadt has a long-standing tradition of poetry and song, and so a long history of building instruments for it. Bards are proud of their songs, and the text imagines the instruments being proud of their owners and that tradition.

302.content: Wine and Song (also: Wine & Song): Wine and Song is a four-star catalyst of the Alley series: an elegantly bound songbook from the aristocratic era, scented with daisies and aged wine, whose composer is forgotten. It holds a popular tavern ballad about a heroic gentleman thief.

303.content: Winter's Heavy Heart (also: Winters Heavy Heart, Secrets of Frost): Winter's Heavy Heart is a four-star catalyst in the Fae series, added in version 7.1. The in-game description calls it a ceremonial artifact formed from the purest ice and snow, which generations of Snegovik lords used in coronations until the Cataclysm five hundred years ago. Its story is about the first Snegovik, a blood-soaked ruler who did not know what love was, and the youth she trained.

304.content:
Witch's Revelation Case (also: Witch's Revelation Case gadget, Barbeloth's case): The Witch's Revelation Case is a gadget the Traveler receives from the seer-witch Barbeloth in Fontaine. It is the key to the Witch's Revelation system: with it, the Traveler can view and accept revelation quests that unlock extra talent effects for certain characters.

Lore: Outside the city of Fontaine the Traveler and Paimon find a fortune-telling booth with a Dodoco in the chair. It is a stand-in through which Barbeloth, a witch of the Hexenzirkel, speaks, joined by her friend Alice. Barbeloth explains that as a Descender the Traveler's fate is not anchored in Teyvat, so most fortune tellers, herself included, cannot read it. She has glimpsed the faces of people tied to an omen, and she wants the Traveler's help gathering them.

305.content:
Wolf-Fang (also: Wolf Fang): Wolf-Fang is a 4-star sword from the Battle Pass Gnostic Hymn of Version 4.0, in-game described as a longsword once used by a wandering knight. Its text explains how the nameless first Knight of Boreas became a legend in early Mondstadt. Released 2023-08-16.

Lore: Mondstadt's knights have, "by coincidence or fate," two distinguished titles and animal insignia: the Lion of the first Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, and the Wolf Knight, Boreas, from almost the same period. In truth, the text says, there is no record at all of the Knight of Boreas; the name comes from stories circulating in the streets.

306.content:
Wolf's Gravestone (also: Wolfs Gravestone): Wolf's Gravestone is a 5-star claymore and, per the wiki, the sword of the first Knight of Boreas, also called the Wandering Knight. Its text tells of a knight and the wolf Boreas who shared one spirit: when the wolf died the knight set the sword over its grave, left Mondstadt and lived as a lone wanderer. Added in Version 1.0.

Lore: The Knight of Boreas's journey ended at the city of Barbatos. As he entered it, his wolf companion said farewell without a sound, since the free-spirited wolf disliked stone walls and lamplight and longed for the wilds.

307.content:
Xiphos' Moonlight (also: Xiphos Moonlight): Xiphos' Moonlight is a 4-star sword: an ancient double-edged blade that glimmers with moonlight, said to hold a now-silent Jinni. Its story is that of Xiphos, a warrior of Tulaytullah, and the exiled wanderer who killed him.

Lore: Thousands of years ago, after the foolish God-King was buried by sandstorms, mortal cities dotted the land. The most outstanding was Tulaytullah, where men and women of wisdom gathered, with sapphire-domed buildings and emerald gardens of blooming trees and fountains. A warrior named Xiphos lived there, adept with his double-edged sword.

Owners: In the story the sword belonged to Xiphos and then to the exiled wanderer who killed him. The wiki notes Nilou, Layla and Alhaitham are shown with it in trailers and quest scenes (Alhaitham in his fight with Cyno), which is not ownership.

308.content:
Yakshas: The Guardian Adepti (also: The Guardian Adepti, Yakshas, The Guardian Adepti): Yakshas: The Guardian Adepti is a single book from the folklore series Hidden Wonders and Folklore of Liyue, Liyue's answer to the Sumeru scholar Masudi's encyclopedia Tour of the Land of Liyue. It was largely dismissed by publishers and readers for its archaic style. It tells how Rex Lapis summoned yakshas to purge daemons, how the five strongest were afflicted, and how only Alatus survived. It is given to the player in the story quest Glimmers of the Vigilant Yaksha (Version 1.3).

Lore: In ancient Liyue plagues and monsters arose from the bitterness of defeated gods, called daemons. Rex Lapis summoned yakshas, ferocious illuminated beasts, to purge them. Five were strongest: Bosacius, Indarias, Bonanus, Menogias and Alatus. Over about a thousand years the yakshas were poisoned by the lingering divine bitterness; three of the five died, one vanished, and only Alatus survived, remembered as the Golden-Winged King and Conqueror of Demons.
